Success in this position requires strong collaboration, adaptability, instructional expertise, and a commitment to advancing excellent teaching and learning for all students. ESSENTIAL QUALIFICATIONS Education, Work Experience, and Knowledge Deep experience coaching educators in grades K-8 special education Experience teaching or coaching HMH Into Reading, EL Education, S.P.I.R.E. Foundations, Aprendo Leyendo, Wilson Reading System, Phonics For Reading, REWARDS, and/or STARI curriculum At least two (2) years of experience as an instructional coach to teachers or school leaders with evidence of impact in student learning outcomes Experience supporting various levels of instruction across classroom settings Strong background in instructional best practices, with the ability to apply strategies that support effective teaching and learning for a wide range of educators and students Experience in designing professional development materials or serving as an instructional designer Experience facilitating impactful professional learning and coaching for educators in both virtual and in-person settings Experience building and managing relationships with diverse stakeholders in an education context Experience empowering teachers through trusting relationships and supporting shifts in practice and mindset to improve student learning Values, Skills, and Competencies Strong commitment to growth mindset for both adults and students, with a desire to continuously strengthen instructional practices and team capabilities Ability to design and deliver high-quality, evidence-based professional learning that advances teaching and learning outcomes Compelling communication and facilitation skills that build engagement and influence across diverse educators and stakeholders Strong organizational skills, with the ability to manage complex projects, multiple priorities, and tight timelines in a fast-paced environment PREFERRED QUALIFICATIONS Expertise in MTSS support and/or bilingual education ABOUT COACHING/FACILITATION ROLES At Teaching Lab, our coaches and facilitators play a vital role in advancing our mission by delivering high-quality professional learning experiences. There is no guarantee of hours. The number of service hours and the specific hours are dependent on the projects we have and when you are available. These roles are project-based and flexible, with opportunities communicated several weeks in advance so you can align them with your schedule. Once assigned, you’ll collaborate with our project teams to prepare, practice, and tailor content to the needs of our partners, ensuring every session is both impactful and engaging. Facilitation may be virtual or in person, and when travel is required, you’ll manage logistics with the support of Teaching Lab’s travel policies. jobs.title: Economist/Statistician (Economics)
jobs.description: The Bureau of Labor Statistics measures labor market activity, working conditions, price changes, and productivity in the U.S. economy to support public and private decision making. The position is located in the Bureau of Labor Statistics, Office of Employment and Unemployment Statistics. This is an interdisciplinary position and may be filled either as an Economist or Statistician (Economics). Qualifications: Basic Requirement Economist, 0110: A) Degree: economics, that included at least 21 semester hours in economics and 3 semester hours in statistics, accounting, or calculus. OR B) Combination of education and experience: courses equivalent to a major in economics, as shown in A above, plus appropriate experience or additional education. Statistician, 1530: A) Degree: that included 15 semester hours in statistics (or in mathematics and statistics, provided at least 6 semester hours were in statistics), and 9 additional semester hours in one or more of the following: physical or biological sciences, medicine, education, or engineering; or in the social sciences including demography, history, economics, social welfare, geography, international relations, social or cultural anthropology, health sociology, political science, public administration, psychology, etc. Credit toward meeting statistical course requirements will be given for courses in which 50 percent of the course content appears to be statistical methods, e.g., courses that included studies in research methods in psychology or economics such as tests and measurements or business cycles, or courses in methods of processing mass statistical data such as tabulating methods or electronic data processing. OR B) Combination of education and experience -- courses as shown in A above, plus appropriate experience or additional education. The experience should have included a full range of professional statistical work such as (a) sampling, (b) collecting, computing, and analyzing statistical data, and (c) applying statistical techniques such as measurement of central tendency, dispersion, skewness, sampling error, simple and multiple correlation, analysis of variance, and tests of significance. jobs.title: Curriculum Development Coordinator
jobs.description: Curriculum Development Coordinator Staff Remote, Lakewood, Colorado Description About the Job The Curriculum Development Coordinator is a non-exempt, full-time position reporting to the Director of Curriculum Development for the College of Adult and Graduate Studies (CAGS). This position works closely with the curriculum development team to manage course development contracting, textbooks, syllabi, service desk work orders, and other general administrative tasks. About CCU Colorado Christian University is the premier interdenominational Christian university in Colorado and the Rocky Mountain region, delivering world class education to thousands of students. The fully accredited, nonprofit University is located in Lakewood, Colorado, a suburb of Denver. Colorado Christian University was founded in 1914 on two principles — grace and truth. CCU’s scriptural foundation comes from John 1:17: For the law was given through Moses; grace and truth came through Jesus Christ. (ESV) CCU's mission is Christ-centered higher education transforming students to impact the world with grace and truth. A leader in higher education, the University has been consistently ranked in the top 2 percent of colleges and universities nationwide for its core curriculum by the American Council of Trustees and Alumni. CCU has had nine consecutive years of enrollment growth and has been named one of the five fastest-growing master’s granting universities by The Chronicle of Higher Education. CCU offers more than 200 degree program options for traditional and adult students through its College of Undergraduate Studies and College of Adult and Graduate Studies. More than 9,000 students attend the University on the main campus, in regional centers throughout Colorado, and online. Scripture states all Christians are called to serve Christ and to minister to others. Because Christians are individuals with different gifts and callings, we serve Christ in a variety of ministry vocations. CCU invites you to explore how you may use your calling and gifts at the University. What is most appealing about working at CCU? Faith-friendly: CCU’s culture is unique to higher education. Where else can you pursue academic excellence yet read the Holy Bible, pray with teammates and students at work, and work to impact our culture in support of Christian values? Convictionally Christian: As a university, we have an enduring commitment to Christ, his kingdom and the truth of God’s Word. Live out your calling: We are a traditional evangelical university where you can invest your God-given talents and abilities alongside coworkers and teammates, while having a profound influence on students as they deepen their relationship with Jesus Christ. Equip students for kingdom work: You can be a part of helping students discover their callings and preparing them for positions of significant leadership in the church, business, government, education, and other professions, as a key part of our University's Strategic Priorities. We’re looking for candidates who have: A bachelor's degree from an accredited college/university is preferred. Knowledge and understanding of Microsoft Office is required Experience with LMS platforms is preferred. Demonstrated organizational, project management, and time management skills. Demonstrated ability to think critically, problem-solve, and have a high attention to detail while maintaining a strategic perspective. Ability to communicate and work effectively with individuals with different backgrounds and levels of expertise. Key Job Duties Contribute to CCU’s mission: CCU provides Christ-centered higher education to transform students to impact the world with grace and truth. The Curriculum Development Coordinator contributes to this mission by assisting the curriculum development team in producing effective materials to serve our students and faculty well. Coordinate the contracting and payment processes for content experts using eForms. Maintain an internal database of active course textbooks. Facilitate the textbook adoption process, including communicating with the school bookstore and notifying the Director of edition updates or textbooks that are difficult to source. Communicate with faculty regarding course textbook needs, provide information on accessing digital textbooks, and request desk copies from publishers as needed. Troubleshoot faculty textbook issues and serve as a primary point of contact when students experience textbook-related challenges. Update course syllabi in Concourse software, maintain archived syllabi, and fulfill requests for archived documents as needed. Organize, respond to, assign, and resolve course fix tickets as appropriate. Maintain a database of course editors and loaders, coordinate course shells for editing and loading, and conduct quality assurance checks on courses submitted by loaders. Monitor and manage multiple email inboxes, ensuring timely responses and appropriate follow-up. Perform other duties as assigned. Work Environment While performing the duties of this job, you may be required to walk, stand, sit, reach with hands and arms, balance, stoop, speak with clarity, and have appropriate vision and hearing capabilities. The employee must occasionally lift and/or move up to 25 pounds. Colorado Christian University expects all faculty and staff to become a part of the University community by participating in activities and events that occur on the campus throughout the year, which may occur during evenings and weekends. What we offer our employees: We offer competitive compensation and benefits packages to all employees. Our benefits package includes a tuition waiver program, excellent healthcare, generous paid time off, a matching 403(b) retirement plan, and additional organizational paid benefits and voluntary benefit offerings. Colorado Christian University’s pay philosophy is based on internal and external data for pay equity; along with budgetary considerations for effective stewardship. Pay will be assigned based on relevant experience at a range of $19.23- $21.63 per hour. We reserve the right to pay an equitable rate that we believe is within our salary structure or that may fit a candidate’s qualifications or experience for the job. A wage range posted is not a guarantee of a specific wage range for a job offer. CCU reserves the right to make pay decisions based on economic and equity considerations to attract the best possible talent. CCU does not determine pay based on sex or any other protected status. Spiritual Requirements Committed follower of Jesus Christ, who believes there is no salvation apart from faith in his atonement on the cross, by grace alone becoming "born again" thus beginning a personal relationship with Christ, the Son of God. Able to effectively communicate personal faith and apply biblical principles and convictions in the workplace. Must have a strong sense of calling to the ministry of Colorado Christian University. Regularly attend and be engaged in meaningful involvement in a Bible-believing evangelical local church. Knowledgeable about the Word of God and passionate about Christian education. Must be a traditional evangelical Christian whose lifestyle is in consonance with sound Christian principles, is compatible with CCU’s Statement of Faith, and is in agreement with the Strategic Priorities promulgated by the University. Review of applications will continue until the position is filled. Colorado Christian University does not discriminate on the basis of race, color, national origin, ethnicity, ancestry, sex, age, physical or mental disability, military or veteran status. CCU is committed to an environment free from discrimination and harassment and calls on every member of the university community to be vigilant in deterring and reporting all violations. CCU does reserve the right to exercise preference on the basis of religion in all of its employment practices. All employees who work at CCU must demonstrate a spiritual testimony consistent with our evangelical mission and follow our lifestyle expectations.

jobs.title: Instructional Designer
jobs.description: Instructional Designer Remote, US About Us InStride Health’s mission is to deliver specialty anxiety and OCD care that works for every kid, teen, young adult, and family who needs it. Through this mission, we are expanding access to insurance-based care, increasing engagement in treatment, and improving treatment outcomes. We are doing this by combining research-backed clinical care and innovative technology to eliminate the major problems with care today: difficulty finding providers, months of waiting to be seen, arduous onboarding processes, and inconsistent use of evidence-based therapies and outcomes tracking. Our vision is to become the nation’s most trusted provider of pediatric anxiety and OCD care. Team InStride Health: Our Core Values Give Heart : We lead with heart, treating patients and their families the way we want our loved ones to be treated. Work Smart : We find smarter ways to solve hard problems and fix the broken mental health system by leveraging technology, diversity of thought, and innovation. Have Humility : We leave our egos at the door, empowering our team to collaborate, celebrate diversity, and adopt a growth mindset. Embrace Community: We all belong. We are in this together, and we never worry alone. We believe in each other and recognize that every voice matters. About the Role We are looking for an Instructional Designer to design, build, and manage learning initiatives for our community of providers, including psychiatrists, therapists, and exposure coaches. As a key member of our Learning and Development team, you will partner with clinical leaders and subject matter experts to turn complex behavioral health protocols into engaging, practical training that strengthens the care our providers deliver to kids, teens, and families. The ideal candidate brings a background in online course creation and project management. This is a fully remote position. Responsibilities: Needs Assessment & Instructional Design Conduct front-end needs analyses with clinical leadership to diagnose performance gaps and define measurable, performance-based learning objectives. Apply adult learning theory and instructional design methodologies (e.g., ADDIE, SAM, Backward Design) to structure modular asynchronous and synchronous training paths. Partner closely with clinical subject matter experts (SMEs) to translate complex behavioral health protocols into digestible, scenario-based learning experiences. Content Development & Multimedia Production Design and develop interactive e-learning modules, job aids, and knowledge checks using Articulate 360 (Storyline and Rise). Script, record, and edit multimedia elements, including video walkthroughs, audio voiceovers, screencasts, and graphic assets, using tools such as Camtasia. Use generative AI tools (e.g., ChatGPT, Claude, AI voiceover platforms) responsibly to accelerate storyboarding, draft scenario scripts, build assessment items, and streamline authoring workflows. Stay current on emerging technologies and trends in digital learning. Measurement, Quality Assurance & Iteration Build assessments that evaluate learner comprehension, retention, and clinical application. Conduct rigorous quality assurance reviews of AI-assisted drafts and finalized modules to confirm clinical accuracy, tone, instructional integrity, and technical functionality before deployment. Gather post-training analytics and learner feedback to continuously refine and improve curriculum assets. Project Management Deliver work against defined project timelines, share regular progress updates with cross-functional partners, and keep project tracking tools (e.g., ClickUp) current in real time. What You Need to Succeed in the Role Bachelor's degree in Education, Instructional Design, Instructional Technology, or a related field. 2+ years of professional experience in instructional design and digital course development, ideally for specialized, technical, or clinical adult audiences. Demonstrated proficiency in rapid e-learning authoring tools (specifically Articulate 360) and video/audio editing software (e.g., TechSmith Camtasia, Audacity, or Adobe Creative Cloud). Solid foundation in adult learning theory, instructional design models, and assessment design (e.g., Bloom's Taxonomy, Kirkpatrick Evaluation Model). Practical experience using generative AI tools to accelerate content ideation, drafting, and multimedia production while maintaining strict editorial and factual oversight. Strong project management and organizational skills. Clear, effective verbal and written communication across remote, multidisciplinary teams. Ability to work well both independently and as part of a collaborative, cross-functional team in a fast-paced, mission-driven environment. Interest or background in behavioral health is a plus. Flexibility and adaptability in a dynamic startup environment: we're looking for candidates who embrace change, thrive in ambiguity, and shift readily as priorities and team needs evolve. A portfolio of past instructional design projects, storyboards, or interactive e-learning modules is required with your application. Salary The expected annual salary for this role is between $72,000–$80,000. Actual starting salary will be determined on an individualized basis and will be based on several factors including but not limited to specific skill set, work experience, etc. Why Join Our Team Generous benefits package (401k with match, Flexible PTO, paid holidays, paid service days, 4 week paid sabbatical, 12 week paid parental leave, health benefits starting on your first day, and more) Opportunity to join a mission-driven company that is changing the landscape of pediatric mental health treatment Chance to make a far-reaching impact by helping children and families access desperately-needed, evidence-based care Opportunity to work with talented and experienced team members who have devoted their lives to solving this problem Fully virtual: work from the comfort of your home with periodic in-person retreats Commitment to Diversity, Equity, Inclusion, & Belonging (DEIB) We want to make our clinical services available for everyone, no matter where you come from, what you look like, or how you identify. To achieve this, we recognize we must continually make progress in building a more diverse, equitable, and inclusive team. Through these efforts, we support two primary objectives at InStride Health: Providing high quality patient care to families. We are in a privileged position to support families during a vulnerable time in their lives. We approach all families and each other with compassion and are most effective as a diverse team where all individuals feel valued, respected, and accepted. Building a mission-driven business that lasts. Specifically, we believe our commitment to a supportive culture improves innovation, decision-making, and efficiency. We invite you to share any additional information about yourself or your experiences that may not be reflected in your CV. Inclusion of this information is completely voluntary. Beware of fake job postings and offers. All official communications from InStride Health will come from email addresses ending in @instride.health. We will never ask for personal information such as Social Security numbers or bank details during the application process. If you receive a suspicious job offer or communication, please contact our recruitment team directly ( talent@instride.health ) to verify its authenticity.

jobs.title: Curriculum Design Specialist, Contract Position
jobs.description: Curriculum Design Specialist, Contract Position About inquirED inquirED was founded by teachers to bring rigorous and joyful learning to every student. We’re a fast-growing start-up, serving more educators and students every day. Inkwell, our integrated ELA and social studies curriculum, brings two core subjects studies together into one coherent instructional experience that builds knowledge and literacy skills, saves time and resources, and supports meaningful learning for both students and teachers. Inquiry Journeys, our elementary social studies curriculum, is used in schools and districts across the country to help students develop deep social studies knowledge and the inquiry skills essential for a thriving democracy. Join our team of designers, advocates, guides, thought leaders, and makers to help us make an even greater impact. Together, we can shape the future of education. About the engagement The Project: We’re building an integrated K–5 Core ELA and social studies curriculum designed to meet the needs of diverse learners while making it easier for elementary teachers to meaningfully incorporate social studies without sacrificing literacy goals. As part of this work, we're looking for part-time Curriculum Design Specialist Contractors to support the ongoing development and refinement of instructional materials. Contractors will work from existing lesson drafts, instructional frameworks, templates, and design guidance to develop and revise complete lessons and individual lesson components. Drawing on their grade-level expertise, they will strengthen standards alignment, student engagement, developmental appropriateness, and accessibility for diverse learners. This engagement focuses on strengthening the clarity, coherence, and instructional quality of curriculum materials. Contractors will collaborate with our curriculum team to incorporate feedback, refine instructional activities, and ensure materials are standards-aligned, engaging, and consistent with inquirED's pedagogical vision. Initial engagement Dec 2026 – March 2027, with potential extension based on project needs. Ideal Candidate Profile: In this contract, you'll collaborate with our curriculum team on a defined scope of deliverables focused on reviewing, revising, and refining elementary instructional materials. You are someone who believes that high-quality curriculum should engage students in meaningful learning while building knowledge and literacy skills. You have a strong understanding of elementary instruction and can recognize what makes a lesson effective, developmentally appropriate, and accessible to diverse learners. You are comfortable working within established curriculum frameworks and using provided models and guidance to revise instructional materials. You welcome feedback, ask thoughtful questions, and collaborate effectively with others to produce clear, engaging, classroom-ready materials. Deliverables: Develop and revise complete lessons and individual lesson components using existing drafts, instructional frameworks, templates, and design guidance. Review lessons and instructional activities in development, providing actionable recommendations to strengthen standards alignment, student engagement, grade-level appropriateness, and accessibility for diverse learners. Ensure instructional materials align with established learning goals, ELA and social studies standards, and unit learning progressions. Apply established instructional strategies, pedagogical approaches, and design specifications to ensure materials are coherent, engaging, and consistent with inquirED's curriculum expectations. Incorporate feedback from curriculum reviewers to improve the clarity, accuracy, and instructional quality of assigned materials. Review and refine materials for completeness, consistency, and classroom usability before submission. Complete assigned deliverables within established timelines, following team workflows and communicating progress, questions, or areas needing clarification as they arise. Qualifications: 4+ years of experience in elementary education, curriculum development, or instructional design, with K–5 classroom teaching experience strongly preferred. Strong understanding of elementary instructional practices, including developmentally appropriate learning activities, student engagement strategies, and scaffolding for diverse learners. Experience developing, reviewing, or revising high- quality instructional materials, including lessons, activities, and student-facing resources. Strong knowledge of elementary ELA or social studies standards and the ability to apply provided standards and learning objectives to evaluate and revise instructional materials. Knowledge of standards in both content areas is preferred. Experience working within established curriculum frameworks, instructional models, and design guidelines to develop or refine instructional materials. Strong attention to detail and ability to incorporate feedback to improve the accuracy, consistency, and instructional quality of materials. Strong organizational and communication skills, with the ability to manage assigned deliverables, meet deadlines, and collaborate effectively with a remote team. Tools You’ll Likely Use: Google Suite and collaborative content development systems (e.g., Airtable) AI content generation and editing platforms (e.g., ChatGPT, Claude, in addition to potential proprietary internal tools) Curriculum tagging systems and rubrics aligned to focus standards Hourly rate for this engagement is $60/hour based on experience. Hours range expected from 10-15 hrs per week based on availability. *Please note that because of high application volume, we are only able to respond to applicants moving forward in the process. Must be U.S. based.

jobs.description: Monitoring, Evaluation and Learning Specialist Fdtn-Office of Philanthropy - Remote, Virginia (Remote) Location Remote, Virginia (Remote) Department Fdtn-Office of Philanthropy Employment Type Regular Full Time About the Internet Society Foundation The Internet Society (ISOC) supports and promotes the development of the Internet as a global technical infrastructure, a resource to enrich people’s lives, and a force for good in society. Our work aligns with our goals for the Internet to be open, globally connected, secure, and trustworthy. We seek collaboration with all who share these goals. Together, we focus on building and supporting the communities that make the Internet work; advancing the development and application of Internet infrastructure, technologies, and open standards; and advocating for policy that is consistent with our view of the Internet. The Internet Society Foundation (Foundation) is a non-profit organization that works in concert with the Internet Society. It exists to demonstrate and support the positive difference the Internet can make to people everywhere and promote the development of the Internet as a global technical infrastructure, a resource to enrich people’s lives, and a force for good in society. The Foundation is committed to a culture of diversity and inclusion, where all individuals are valued for their distinct contributions. Our people are the most valuable strengths we have. The collective sum of the individual differences, life experiences, knowledge, inventiveness, innovation, self-expression, unique capabilities and talent that our staff invests in their work represents a significant part of not only our culture, but our reputation and the Foundation's achievements. About the Position The Monitoring, Evaluation and Learning (MEL) Specialist plays a critical role in supporting the Foundation team as we advance our systems. This position works closely and collaboratively with members of the Philanthropy and Empowerment teams and directly supports the Director, Learning, Evaluation & Impact in ensuring that programs and funded projects are collecting data, supporting analysis efforts to identify results achieved, communicating results, and facilitating learning from data collected. The MEL Specialist will also contribute to the Foundation's capacity building efforts for staff and grantees, particularly in designing and conducting trainings on monitoring, evaluation and learning for staff and partners. The MEL Specialist combines a working knowledge of technical MEL practices with excellent communication and collaboration skills. The Foundation is a small team of passionate, collaborative, and driven staff that depend on each other to move our mission forward; this is true of this critical position. The MEL Specialist will collaborate across the program portfolio, manage multiple priorities, and support internal and external stakeholders. This role requires strong communication, adaptability, and the ability to thrive in a dynamic, globally diverse environment. A track record of teamwork, initiative, and resourcefulness is essential. jobs.title: Analyst, Data
jobs.description: Analyst, Data Operations - United States (Remote) Analyst, Data OPPORTUNITY Nationally recognized nonprofit venture philanthropy seeks to hire an analyst to provide strategic and operational capacity across teams to lead grantmaking. ORGANIZATION NewSchools is a venture philanthropy that builds a better education system by connecting people, resources, and ideas. We bridge the gap between those with capital and those with the courage to put that capital to work on the frontlines of K-12 education. We envision an education system that keeps its promise to all students. That’s why we invest in the ideas and energy of education leaders and entrepreneurs who are advancing innovative solutions that expand the definition of what works. There’s a better way to advance education through philanthropy—one that is more equitable, more collaborative, and more courageous–and we’re proving it every day. RESPONSIBILITIES We seek to hire a Data Analyst to own data stewardship, quality and analytics within the Operations function and assigned to a designated investment team. Reporting to Jessica Henry, Senior Director of Operations, with a dotted line to your assigned investment team (a program team responsible for identifying, funding and supporting education ventures). You will own execution within the data framework and standards designed centrally, while serving as the analytics partner your investment team turns to for reliable data and strategic insight. NewSchools is a fully remote organization, and you may live anywhere in the United States. This role requires up to 10% travel for in-person team meetings, retreats, and conferences. In this role, you will: Own the data and metrics that demonstrate impact for a designated investment team (30%) In partnership with the Data Manager, investment team leads, and the Research & Learning team, translate learning agendas into documented metric definitions, data structures, and processes and translate these into clear stakeholder communications In partnership with the Data Manager, develop and maintain processes that ensure the investment team collects cohesive quantitative and qualitative data specific to key metrics of success — logic model, learning agenda, and funder-facing impact Partner with the Research & Learning team to elevate metrics that support the broader research strategy Identify where business questions can't be answered with existing data or tools; develop well-reasoned recommendations for warehouse additions, public data infrastructure, self-service tool improvements, and research agenda priorities Maintain active working knowledge of NewSchools' full data stack — warehouse, BI tools, and public data infrastructure — to credibly advise the investment team(s) and inform infrastructure decisions Ensure the data feeding into our systems is accurate, complete, and trustworthy from the point of intake (30%) Project manage annual data collection cycles; partner with the Data Manager and investment team leads on clean rostering, survey development, and administration Manage all data intake for the designated investment team(s) — applications, diligence, grantee surveys, internally generated data — including validation processes that catch errors at the source Partner with the data engineer and fellow analysts to validate and clean incoming data and execute automated quality control checkpoints Review and update databases within the designated investment team's scope, ensuring accuracy and integrity across all data sources Apply and reinforce best practices for capturing data updates regularly and accurately within the investment team Spot and report data anomalies from the stakeholder lens — quality issues automated back-end processing may miss — investigate root cause, report to relevant teammates, and manage stakeholder communications when a resolution isn't immediately possible Turn data into the insights and recommendations that shape investment decisions (30%) Own the analytics relationship for your designated investment team(s), developing deep knowledge of its goals, workflows, and data needs to serve as a trusted, actively sought-out resource Lead ad hoc analyses to support data-driven decision-making and synthesize findings into written investment recommendations Own and respond to data reporting and analysis requests supporting grant and funder reporting Manage and execute ad hoc analysis and rapid prototyping using SQL, BI tools, and AI-assisted analytics to answer business questions Collaborate with Research & Learning and investment teams on custom queries and datasets supporting the learning agenda, team strategy, Board requests, and funder reporting and prospecting Develop planning tools, analysis frameworks, and visualizations that drive insight generation and identify portfolio bright spots, accounting for historical, contextual, and comparative data and perspectives Help colleagues across NewSchools find, trust, and use data themselves (10%) Serve as the go-to resource for data questions across the organization, helping non-technical colleagues navigate systems and dashboards Support implementation and adoption of self-service analytics tools across the assigned investment team(s), including onboarding, coaching, and ongoing support Support ad hoc data needs across the organization QUALIFICATIONS Minimum 2 years of experience in roles working with complex data sets and owning end-to-end data processes (collection, auditing, analysis, meaning-making) Proficiency in SQL and experience with cloud data warehouse platforms (BigQuery preferred) Experience with BI/analytics tools (Omni Analytics preferred) and building self-service artifacts and reporting for non-technical users Experience with data validation, quality control processes, and data cleaning Project management experience, particularly running recurring data collection cycles that involve coordinating multiple internal and external stakeholders Comfort using AI-assisted analytics tools for ad hoc analysis and rapid prototyping Knowledge of the K-12 education sector with experience working with teacher, leader, and edtech data -or- Knowledge of the K-12 education sector with experience working with charter and district school and student data strongly preferred Travel up to 10% for in-person team meetings, retreats and conferences EXPERIENCE YOU BRING Building and maintaining knowledge management structures that make portfolio data and findings reusable across teams Supporting progress monitoring and research partnerships, including what gets collected and how data quality is protected Translating analysis into clear insights and recommendations for various stakeholders and audiences Implementing continuous improvement initiatives that increase efficiency Planning, prioritizing and managing multiple workstreams YOUR WAYS OF WORKING Ground decisions, priorities, and actions in NewSchools’ mission and commitment to equity Communicate clearly and proactively, share information before being asked, and raise questions and concerns directly Adapt how you communicate to the audience, make a clear case for your recommendations, and give and receive feedback directly Collaborate across teams, build relationships, and share ideas and insights Set clear priorities, manage competing demands, and keep systems that make prioritization possible Proactively name when an approach isn’t working and propose what to do instead, including reworking or stopping your own workstreams Operate comfortably with imperfect or incomplete data, using sound judgment to deliver useful analysis despite gaps or inconsistencies Apply sound judgment about when to make independent decisions and when to involve someone else Maintain an active view of the field and market through regular scanning of research, data and public sources, and use it to surface patterns and gaps the team should examine COMPENSATION A competitive compensation package including base salary, performance bonus, and employer-funded benefits is available. The starting salary range is $83,000 to $104,000 with the potential for an annual bonus of up to 5%. Final salary will be determined based on experience level and qualifications. Applications submitted by November 6th will receive priority review. We encourage interested candidates to apply early, as the position may close once we’ve received a strong pool of applicants. NewSchools Venture Fund has a strong commitment to diversity. Candidates of all backgrounds are encouraged to apply. Please note, applicants must be authorized to work for any employer in the U.S. We are unable to sponsor or take over sponsorship of an employment visa at this time.

jobs.title: Instructional Designer
jobs.description: Instructional Designer Corporate Full Time Remote PTS US Remote - United States The Instructional Designer designs, develops, implements, and evaluates learning experiences that strengthen employee performance and support clinical excellence. Using the ADDIE model and Understanding by Design framework, this role partners with stakeholders and subject matter experts to assess learning needs and performance gaps, then independently determines the instructional approach, learning objectives, assessments, and activities for assigned projects. The Instructional Designer manages multiple projects, develops online and instructor-led training, and uses learner feedback and assessment results to improve training effectiveness. Essential Functions Analysis Conducts needs assessments with stakeholders, including observations of employees performing job tasks, to identify business needs, learner needs, and performance gaps. Evaluates assessment findings and recommends instructional solutions that support employee performance and clinical excellence. Collaborates with stakeholders and the Sr. Manager of Clinical Education to establish project scope and deliverables Design Independently determines learning objectives, assessments, and instructional activities for assigned projects using Understanding by Design principles. Evaluates and selects instructional methods, delivery formats, and learning assets that support learner engagement, application, and retention. Reviews proposed designs with stakeholders and the Sr. Manager of Clinical Education to confirm alignment with project goals and content requirements. Development Partners with subject matter experts to research, develop, and refine accurate, relevant instructional content. Creates learning materials, practice exercises, knowledge checks, course assessments, and skills checklists aligned with learning objectives. Selects and integrates appropriate learning technologies and interactive elements to support instructional goals. Coordinates stakeholder and supervisor reviews, evaluates and incorporates feedback, and documents required approvals. Implementation Builds, tests, and publishes approved learning content using authoring software and the learning management system. Conducts train-the-trainer sessions to prepare facilitators to deliver instructional content effectively. Coordinates the distribution of approved learning materials to facilitators, stakeholders, and other project participants. Evaluation Evaluates training effectiveness using learner feedback, assessment results, and skills checklist outcomes. Determines and implements appropriate instructional revisions based on evaluation findings and changing business or learner needs. Maintains training content and curricula to ensure accuracy, relevance, and alignment with learning objectives. Project Management and Partnership Manages multiple assigned training projects from analysis through evaluation, using established project management tools and processes. Coordinates content development, review, and approval timelines with subject matter experts and stakeholders; communicates progress and escalates risks or delays. Advises stakeholders on instructional strategies and the effective application of training materials in the field. Maintains collaborative relationships with project teams, subject matter experts, the learning management system provider, and other vendors. Partners with training colleagues to maintain consistent messaging, reuse relevant content, and improve development efficiency. Evaluates and recommends improvements to instructional standards, development processes, and training solutions. Required Skills & Abilities Proficient in authoring tools including Articulate Rise, Articulate Storyline, HeyGen, and video editing. Ability to translate complex information into clear, engaging learning materials. Strong organizational and project management skills, including the ability to manage multiple projects and meet deadlines. Ability to collaborate effectively with employees at all levels of the organization, subject matter experts, and external vendors. Ability to interpret learner feedback and assessment results to improve training effectiveness. Ability to troubleshoot course functionality, organize digital files and learning assets, and publish and maintain content in a learning management system. Required Credentials Bachelor’s degree, preferably in Instructional Design, Learning Design, Educational Technology, Education with formal instructional design training, or a related field. 1-3 years of experience designing and developing instructional content. Experience developing learning content for social media or managing content in a knowledge management platform preferred. Experience developing learning content for social media or managing content in a knowledge management platform preferred. Our commitment to you is evident in our industry-leading professional development opportunities. From ongoing evidence-based clinical education to dedicated mentorship opportunities and an APTA-accredited Orthopedic Residency Program, we propel our clinicians toward excellence in physical therapy, occupational therapy, speech-language pathology, and athletic training. PT Solutions has been named a 2026 USA Today Top Workplace for the fifth consecutive year, based entirely on employee feedback. We’ve also earned five Culture Excellence Awards for Innovation, Professional Development, Work-Life Flexibility, Appreciation, and Purpose & Values. This recognition reflects a culture built around supporting our people. It’s not just what we do, but how we make people feel. Through human connection, intentional care, and being all in for one another, we create experiences that make a difference. Because together, we do great better. Let’s go further together and transform care. Join the #PTSLife today! To see what #PTSLife is like, visit Instagram , Facebook, and LinkedIn . We are an equal opportunity employer and welcome all qualified candidates to apply!

jobs.title: Partner, School Design - Assessment
jobs.description: Start Date: Immediate Role Type: Full-time Reports to: David Nitkin, Managing Partner Team: Evidence Location/Travel: Remote (U.S.-based); willingness to travel approximately once per month, ~30% travel Who We Are Transcend is a national nonprofit that helps communities reimagine and redesign schools so every young person can thrive in a rapidly changing world. Across the country, communities are recognizing that classrooms built for the industrial age aren’t preparing learners for what’s next. Instead, schools must be designed for continuous evolution: relevant, resilient, and ready for the future. For more than a decade, Transcend has partnered with school and system leaders to build the capacity for bold, lasting change—change led by the people who live it every day. We’ve worked with nearly 500 schools and 200 districts serving over 225,000 students in 35 states. Together, we’ve seen what’s possible when communities lead redesign with proven methods, insight, and support. From that work, we develop and share tools, research, and models that help schools everywhere make the leap to extraordinary learning—for every child, in every community. For more information, visit our website or follow us on LinkedIn . The Opportunity The purpose of Transcend's Evidence team is to make it possible for extraordinary learning communities to understand and communicate their impact. Unfortunately the most predominant tools for measuring that impact, standardized tests in English Language Arts and math, have significant limitations. These tests capture only a slice of what matters most, leaving higher-order skills like critical thinking, complex problem-solving, and collaboration largely unmeasured. They are built on the assumption that all students progress and learn at the same pace, making personalized and competency-based learning difficult to implement while creating significant logistical burdens for students and teachers. Part of Transcend's mission is to help change that reality, pushing the field toward new and better forms of assessment. The Partner, School Design - Assessment will work at the center of that challenge. This role will work directly with schools and districts to help them pilot, validate, and scale innovative assessment approaches that are more personalized, less administratively burdensome, and able to measure a wider range of outcomes and experiences than the current systems allow. In particular, we believe there is significant promise in assessments that combine proven practices such as portfolio- and performance-based assessments with new possibilities enabled by AI. This role sits at the intersection of psychometrics and school design, requiring someone who can translate technical rigor into practical guidance for educators and facilitate the kind of community-driven design that builds genuine ownership. To hear more about the role, the work, and the team, please watch this video from David Nitkin . Key Responsibilities As a Partner, School Design - Assessment on the Evidence team, you will work closely with school and district teams through design journeys focused on piloting, implementing, and strengthening innovative assessment practices and tools. You will support communities across the country as they build shared vision; align instruction and systems; and move from design into piloting and implementation — while contributing to a collaborative project team committed to learning, iteration, and meaningful impact. You’ll be a project lead, taking on ownership of a complex project from end to end. You work with the Managing Partner to define what success looks like, align the work and any team members to get there, manage the conditions for a thriving partner relationship and team culture, and take on increasing external stakeholder management alongside your manager. This will include: Leading project planning and execution: Define overall project success, including milestones, deliverables, and metrics. Build a clear project plan aligned to goals, Transcend's core schema, and local context. Manage project expenses to the approved budget and communicate progress to ensure timeline, quality delivery. Building and leading your project team: Foster a project team culture where members do their best work. Put clear collaboration and communication structures in place, ensure role and work clarity, and create opportunities to reinforce Transcend's values, mission, and equity commitments. Managing external relationships: Support the cultivation and stewardship of school partners, funders, and system leaders. This may also include supporting your manager with scoping for prospective projects and grants. Contributing to ongoing learning: As you work across schools and districts, you’ll contribute to the Evidence team’s collective learning about the future of assessment and accountability systems. You will also share your experiences working on the ground with school and system leaders with internal and external audiences to showcase examples of innovative assessment practices in action. Sample projects that you would lead: Piloting uses of AI in literacy assessment: Partner with two secondary schools to pilot AI-augmented literacy assessment embedded in real classrooms. You would convene diverse design teams of students, educators, and administrators to identify high-leverage use cases; pilot new approaches; and document implementation lessons that other schools can follow. This project would help define what responsible, high-impact AI use in literacy assessment actually looks like in practice, establish credible proof points, and help spur broader, responsible adoption of AI to strengthen literacy assessment at scale. Revamping accountability systems for a charter authorizer: Generate recommendations for updating a charter authorizer’s high school accountability plan framework and accompanying progress reporting systems to align with a statewide Portrait of a Graduate. You would conduct a national scan of how charter authorizers and state systems are evolving their approaches to high school accountability to encompass holistic student outcomes; directly engage school leaders to understand current practices and invite them to engage with examples of how schools nationally are assessing complex competencies and concrete tools and resources they can adapt for their own communities; and co-develop with the authorizer a clear, actionable proposal for evolving their approach to high school accountability, including recommended updates to measures, evidence sources, reporting structures, and evaluation protocols. Facilitate workshops where schools explore and apply a Portrait of a Graduate to their context: Help schools unpack a state Portrait of a Graduate and apply it to their local contexts, providing supporting resources and considering how they may gather evidence against it. You would design and facilitate a workshop where school leaders leave with an understanding of what’s required of their school and students as it relates to implementing the Portrait; how the competencies align with their school’s model and community; and how they might gather evidence towards the Portrait competencies. Who You Are You are a leader who lives at the intersection of psychometrics and school design, energized by the challenge of making assessment more meaningful, more personalized, and less burdensome for students and educators. You move comfortably between big-picture strategy and the day-to-day details of a multi-site, traveling role, staying organized across multiple workstreams while adapting as plans evolve. You build trust easily with a wide range of stakeholders and bring the political acumen to navigate complex dynamics with discernment and care. And to all of this, you bring: A deep commitment to Transcend’s mission of transforming education and a passion for designing learning experiences where all students thrive. Curiosity, care, and a drive to make meaningful change —living into Transcend’s values through how you work, connect, and lead. A genuine curiosity about the possibilities AI creates for assessment , tempered by the discipline to test rigorously before scaling anything new. Prior experience directly implementing K-12 assessments in schools in which you've seen firsthand what works, what doesn't, and where the field's biggest opportunities lie. A robust foundational knowledge of core psychometric principles (e.g., validity, reliability, comparability, bias), and the ability to translate that technical rigor into practical, everyday guidance for educators. Strong facilitation skills and a knack for leading inclusive, engaging design experiences: the kind that builds genuine shared vision, ownership, and momentum with the school and district teams you partner with. An R&D orientation , you're energized by learning, iterating, and improving your approach over time, both within your project team and alongside the communities you support. Outstanding project management and organizational skills , with the ability to juggle multiple workstreams and keep the logistics of a traveling, multi-site role running smoothly. Strong self-management skills, including comfort navigating ambiguity , structuring your own time, and adapting as plans shift, all without losing sight of the bigger picture. Skill and care in building relationships across a wide range of stakeholders , including students, families, teachers, school leaders, district leaders, and funders. Resourcefulness and a solutions-oriented mindset ,especially when conditions are complex, evolving, or imperfect, you are able to find the practical path forward. A willingness to travel approximately 30% of the time (roughly once a month) to work directly with the school and district partners you support. And above all, you care deeply about getting assessment right for students , pushing past the limits of standardized tests toward approaches that reflect the fuller range of what students know and can do. Application & Hiring Process We review applications on a rolling basis and are committed to a thoughtful and people-centered hiring experience that helps candidates understand what it’s like to work at Transcend. Here’s a sample hiring process at Transcend; though the stages for this individual role may vary: Initial interview with the team via Zoom to learn more about your interest and experiences. Try-on activity to engage in a role-aligned exercise. This helps us get a sense of how you approach the work and gives you a feel for what the role might be like. Interviews with the team, where you will meet with a small group of Transcend teammates with whom you are likely to collaborate with in the role. Final round interviews with two senior leaders at Transcend, including the Managing Partner, David Nitkin. Reference checks to learn more about your superpowers and working style. Salary As a national team, we apply a cost-of-labor adjustment by adjusting salaries into 3 geographical bands (geo-band) in order to offer competitive compensation for all employees across the US. These geo-bands help us tailor compensation appropriately based on the specific location of each teammate. Below are the three salary geo-bands for this role, and we will confirm the individual range for your location during this initial interview, if you move forward in the process. Geo Comp 1: Currently Includes: NYC metro area, CA Bay Area, Boston City, LA City, Washington, D.C, Seattle $145,000 - $210,000 Geo Comp 2: Currently includes locations such as: San Diego; New Haven, CT; Ventura, CA $137,750 - $199,500 Geo Comp 3: Currently Includes: Most other US locations $130,500 - $189,000 A Few Nuts & Bolts We are an experienced team focused on extraordinary learning for all. We welcome candidates who are passionate about ensuring that all students thrive. We are also committed to providing our colleagues with a competitive benefits package a

jobs.title: Clinical Lab Scientist
jobs.description: This position is eligible for the Education Debt Reduction Program (EDRP), a student loan payment reimbursement program. You must meet specific individual eligibility requirements in accordance with VHA policy and submit your EDRP application within four months of appointment. Program Approval, award amount (up to $200,000) and eligibility period (one to five years) are determined by the VHA Education Loan Repayment Services program office after complete review of the EDRP application. Qualifications: Applicants pending the completion of educational or certification/licensure requirements may be referred and tentatively selected but may not be hired until all requirements are met. Basic Requirements: United States Citizenship: Non-citizens may only be appointed when it is not possible to recruit qualified citizens in accordance with VA Policy. English Language Proficiency: Candidates must be proficient in spoken and written English in accordance with 38 U.S.C. § 7403 (f) Education: A bachelor's degree or higher from an accredited college or university. Foreign Education. To be creditable, education completed outside the U.S. must be deemed at least equivalent to that gained in a conventional U.S. program by a private organization specializing in the interpretation of foreign educational credentials. Graduates of foreign baccalaureate degree programs meet the educational requirements if they meet either of the following: Foreign transcripts are evaluated by an acceptable evaluation agency, and the degree is found to be equivalent to a NAACLS-approved U.S. clinical laboratory science degree program. OR The applicant submits a letter from ASCP BOC or AMT stating the individual is eligible to take the certification examination. NOTE: Possession of a certification identified below automatically determines the foreign education as creditable and no further documentation or proof of equivalency is needed. Certification: Candidates must meet one of the certification options below. Generalist certification as an MLS given by ASCP BOC or AMT. Generalist certification as an MT given by ASCP BOR or AMT. Categorical certification or Specialist certification by ASCP or AMT. NOTE: Categorical and specialist certifications are not acceptable for CLS Generalist positions or lab sections unrelated to the categorical or specialist certification held. Categorical or specialist certifications are acceptable for higher-graded positions within the relevant lab section or one of the non-section specific assignments (including, Ancillary Testing Coordinator, Education Coordinator, Laboratory Information Manager, Quality Manager, Laboratory Manager, Regional Technical Specialist, National Quality and Compliance Agent, Regional Program Manager, Regional Director, Laboratory Director, or National Quality and Compliance Officer). May qualify based on being covered by the Grandfathering Provision as described in the VA Qualification Standard for this occupation (only applicable to current VHA employees who are in this occupation and meet the criteria). GS-11 Grade Determination: Experience: 1 year of creditable experience equivalent to the next lower grade level. OR Education. Must have 3 full years of progressively higher-level graduate education or a Ph.D. or equivalent doctoral degree in medical technology or a directly related science. AND Knowledge, Skills, and Abilities: In addition to the experience above, the candidate must demonstrate the following KSAs: Knowledge of professional clinical laboratory science principles, practices, concepts, and theories that support sound, independent work. Knowledge of laboratory quality control and quality assurance procedures and principles of performance improvement. Skill in informatics, laboratory data flow, and laboratory processes. Ability to maintain, troubleshoot, and repair instrumentation. Ability to use independent technical judgment to analyze and interpret laboratory results. Ability to read, interpret, and apply complex written instructions. Ability to communicate, consult, and interact with other members of the health care team, external relations, customer service, and patient education. Preferred Experience: 2-5 years of experience as a CLS Generalist covering all sections in Lab including Blood bank, Chemistry/UA, Hem/Coag, Microbiology/Molecular, Quality Management, and other related duties as assigned. Understanding of regulatory compliance and Quality Management. Reference: For more information on this qualification standard, please visit https://www.va.gov/ohrm/QualificationStandards/. The full performance level of this vacancy is GS-11. Physical Requirements: See VA Directive and Handbook 5019, Employee Occupational Health Service for requirements.

jobs.title: Revenue Systems Analyst
jobs.description:
About Amplify

Amplify helps teachers bring delight and rigor to students every day. We have become a leader in K–12 literacy, biliteracy, math, and science by building inspiring teaching and learning experiences based on research. The Amplify Classroom platform combines curriculum, assessment, and supplemental learning into one coherent high-quality instructional system. A pioneer in education since 2000, Amplify has developed deep relationships in states and districts by partnering with educators to drive implementation quality and improved outcomes. Today, Amplify serves more than 18 million students and teachers across all 50 states and on six continents. For more information, visit Amplify.com http://amplify.com.



Description:

The Revenue Systems Analyst is the connective tissue between Revenue Systems, the overall Revenue Operations team, and the Business Systems team. This role leads structured process discovery, maps current and future state workflows, and translates operational needs into clear, testable requirements for Business Systems and other partners, with a focus on business clarity rather than system configuration. The focus of the Revenue Systems team is improving seller and sales-operations execution across lead-to-cash (quoting, contracting, ordering, invoicing, renewals/amendments), reducing rework, strengthening data integrity, sales finance/ budgeting, and accelerating change adoption.

This role also supports the strategy, administration, and adoption of the platforms that power revenue workflows, including our market intelligence platform. Success in this role depends less on producing documents than on the human work behind them, building trust with business partners, asking the questions that surface what people actually do versus what the process says they do, and driving decisions across teams that don't always agree. This is not a system administration or configuration role.



Essential Responsibilities:



Business Process Discovery and Design

 - Facilitate workshops and working sessions with key stakeholders (Account Executives, District Managers, Sales Support, Renewals, Sales Finance, and Business Systems) to document current state end-to-end business processes and define improved future state designs facilitated by systems and process improvements.

 - Create clear, multi-level process maps (e.g., lead-to-quote, quote-to-contract, order-to-cash, renewals/amendments) that reflect real seller and operations workflows, handoffs, approvals, and exception paths.

 - Establish and maintain a lightweight process library (maps, SOPs, definitions, decision trees) so institutional knowledge is durable and scalable.

Requirements and Solution Definition (Sales and Sales Operations Lens)

 - Translate process and policy decisions into well-structured requirements: user stories, acceptance criteria, business rules, and operational scenarios - ensuring clarity, completeness, and testability.

 - Partner with Business Systems to validate feasibility, clarify ambiguities, and ensure requirements reflect both the operational intent and system constraints.

 - Maintain traceability from process maps -> requirements -> test cases -> release notes to reduce rework and ensure end-to-end quality.

 - Use AI-powered tools (e.g., Glean, Claude, Gemini) to accelerate drafting of user stories, business cases, acceptance criteria, process documentation, and stakeholder synthesis — applying judgment to validate accuracy, completeness, and business fit rather than accepting output at face value.

Tools Strategy and Administration

 - Support the administration and strategy development of the platforms supporting revenue workflows, including our market intelligence platform, assisting in configuration, user access, adoption tracking, and vendor coordination.

 - Translate market intelligence signals into usable seller and sales-operations workflows, partnering with Business Systems on data flow, attribution, and reporting integration.

 - Build and maintain enablement resources (playbooks, prompt libraries, use case guides) that drive consistent, high-value usage across the field.

 - Evaluate, pilot, and operationalize additional platforms as needed, including AI-enabled solutions, and make recommendations on fit, sequencing, and expansion.

Operational Readiness, Testing, and Change Enablement

 - Co-design UAT approaches and test scenarios rooted in real-world seller and Sales Operations use cases; coordinate execution with Business Systems and key business testers.

 - Develop end-user documentation (job aids, playbooks, process guides) and support enablement activities to drive adoption and consistent execution.

 - Support release readiness by confirming training, communications, reporting impacts, and operational 'go-live' checklists are complete.

Continuous Improvement and Performance Insights

 - Use operational data and qualitative feedback to identify friction points, bottlenecks, policy leakage, and process variability - and recommend improvements.

 - Support defining process KPIs (cycle time, rework/defect rates, adoption, SLA attainment) and partner with reporting teams to surface actionable insights.

 - Promote standardization and simplification while preserving necessary state/district/contracting complexity through clear guardrails and exception handling.

 - Evaluate emerging technologies, automation opportunities, and AI-enabled solutions that can simplify workflows, reduce manual effort, and improve operational effectiveness.

Cross-Functional Partnership and Governance

 - Act as a neutral facilitator to align Sales, Finance, and Business Systems on process decisions, definitions, and sequencing - especially in quoting, contracting, ordering, and invoicing workflows.

 - Support governance routines (change intake, prioritization, documentation standards, decision logs) to keep cross-functional work moving and reduce 'spin.'

 - Contribute to program initiatives across the revenue systems roadmap (e.g., quoting modernization, amendments/contracting improvements, data governance, commission and budget operationalization, seller enablement).

Minimum Qualifications:

 - Bachelor's degree in Business, Operations, or related field (or equivalent experience).

 - 4+ years of experience in Sales Operations, Revenue Operations, Business Process Analysis, or related roles focused on process design and operational improvement.

 - Demonstrated ability to create process maps and documentation that non-technical audiences can follow (e.g., Lucidchart, Visio, Miro, or similar).

 - Experience translating business needs into clear requirements (user stories, acceptance criteria, business rules) and supporting cross-functional delivery.

 - Experience working with CRM and revenue operations platforms (Salesforce preferred) and familiarity with lead-to-cash processes including quoting, contracting, ordering, invoicing, and renewals.

 - Strong facilitation, stakeholder management, and written communication skills; comfortable driving alignment across teams with competing priorities.

 - Analytical mindset and comfort using data to diagnose issues and validate improvements.

jobs.description: Summary About the Team and the Program The Pathway Gap Data and Systems Coordinator works within the Department of Community Engagement and Postsecondary Pathways (CEPP) at New Visions for Public Schools. Our vision is that every young person in New York City can clearly see, navigate, and access best-fit career pathways, supported by shared civic infrastructure that helps the adults advising them guide the way. Reporting to the Associate Director of Pathway Gap, the Data Coordinator plays a key role in the success of the Pathway Gap Initiative —a cross-sector collaboration of more than 75 organizations designed to address the systemic challenges that make it difficult for youth-serving professionals to connect young people to postsecondary and workforce opportunities. For more information on the Pathway Gap project, please see this project overview . About the Role The role owns the accuracy, completeness, and timeliness of the program data that powers the New Visions Career Directory. The main focus for the first two years of the role is launching the project’s new Training Dates solution—a not-yet-built system for surfacing real-time training program dates and application deadlines, and ensuring young people have an actionable next step. Because the Training Dates solution is a new effort, this role will be central to its earliest stages: Piloting the data collection process with a small initial cohort of training providers (~30 programs) Identifying and troubleshooting issues as they arise Helping shape what it takes to scale the approach in future phases Working closely with the Associate Director of Pathway Gap to liaise with the technology team, translating pilot learnings into clear design requirements Beyond the pilot, you'll work directly with workforce training providers to collect, verify, and maintain program information—building the kind of trusted relationships that keep data accurate as programs evolve. This role is a great fit if you enjoy direct outreach to external partners, research, and data quality work; are comfortable with ambiguity; enjoy problem-solving in a developing system; can bring structure and rigor to a new process; and want your day-to-day work to translate into real opportunities for young people across New York City. Core Responsibilities 1. Training Dates Solution: Pilot & Scaling Pilot Cohort Coordination: Serve as the primary point of contact for the initial pilot cohort of organizations, representing approximately 30 programs, guiding them through the new data submission process to guarantee data completeness, clarifying data requirements, and ensuring clear communication around the strategic goals of this initiative. Process Troubleshooting & User Testing: Identify friction points, data gaps, and breakdowns in the data collection process as they emerge—troubleshooting issues directly with providers and flagging systemic problems to the Associate Director of Pathway Gap and technology team. Participate in user acceptance testing for product features before and after launch to curate and elevate feedback and concerns. Scaling Refinement: Contribute pilot-informed recommendations on what's needed to refine and scale the solution beyond the initial cohort, based on provider and user pain points, inclusive of process and workflow changes, automation and process optimization opportunities, collection of additional data points central to the initiative, and continuous improvement ahead of subsequent rollouts. Help the team identify opportunities for greater efficiency and consistency as the number of participating programs grows, and use feedback to inform reporting to the Associate Director of Pathway Gap and funders. 2. Directory & Systems Maintenance Career Directory Content Maintenance and Verification Audits: Update program information directly within the Career Directory's content management system, ensuring listings are current, properly formatted, and reflect the most recent verified data. Conduct scheduled audits of existing program listings to confirm that programs are still active, accurately, described, and correctly categorized. Identify and resolve inconsistencies, outdated information, or gaps in program data, applying close attention to detail to maintain a high bar for accuracy across the Directory. Data Outreach: Proactively reach out to providers via phone and email to request updated information, clarify details, and follow up on outstanding data needs, balancing persistence with professionalism. Respond to provider questions and concerns about how their program information appears in the Directory, as well as Directory data standards, and escalate more complex issues to the Associate Director of Pathway Gap as needed. New Program Sourcing and Research: Research and source information for new training programs to be added to the Career Directory, ensuring all required fields are complete, accurate, and consistent with established data standards. 3. Relationship Management Partner Engagement: Build and maintain strong, trusted working relationships with workforce training providers, serving as solutions-oriented point of contact for data collection and program updates. Feedback Loops: Solicit ongoing feedback from training providers about the data collection process itself—identifying friction points, unclear requirements, or process improvements that would make it easier for providers to keep their information current. Relay provider feedback to the Pathway Gap and technology teams to inform future tool and process improvements. Cross-Team Coordination: Coordinate with the broader Pathway Gap and technology teams to relay provider feedback that may inform future improvements to data collection tools and processes. Committee mobilization: Partner with the project lead to manage the operations of the cross-organizational Quality and Standards Committee, including leading relevant monthly subcommittees, and supporting the planning and execution of three annual in-person convenings. Qualifications Required Education and Experience Education: Bachelor’s degree or equivalent blending of academic and applied experience. Professional Experience: 2-4 years of experience in operations, program support, content management, or a related field. Data Collection + Quality Assurance Experience : Demonstrated experience compiling and maintaining accurate, well-organized data sets, including spotting inconsistencies and resolving discrepancies. External Communication: Experience conducting outreach and communicating with external partners or providers via phone and email to gather or verify information. Familiarity with the NYC workforce development ecosystem , including training providers, career pathways programs, and the types of credentials and outcomes they offer, strongly preferred. Required Knowledge and Skills Strong attention to detail, with the ability to verify information against source materials and maintain high data accuracy across a large, frequently changing data set. A friendly, persistent, solutions-oriented approach to building and sustaining relationships with both new and known external partners. Ability to listen actively, ask clarifying questions, follow through independently, and know when to escalate. Comfort with ambiguity and shifting practices: energized rather than thrown off by the early-stage nature of a new initiative, with ability to bring structure and patience to shifting operational workflows and still-developing processes to and help shape what scaling should look like. Comfort working alongside a technology team and contributing stakeholder perspective to product development processes; proficiency with standard productivity and data tools. (e.g., Google Workspace, spreadsheet); experience with content management systems or databases to organize and track information preferred. Physical requirements Ability to traverse an office environment to attend meetings and interact with colleagues Ability to operate a computer and other relevant technology, such as phones, screens, printers, and tablets Ability to remain in a stationary position for extended periods, as is common in office settings Ability to communicate and exchange accurate information with internal and external stakeholders Ability to travel to partner organizations across the 5 boroughs on a periodic basis Ability to carry up to 10 pounds (such as for a laptop and carrying case) Candidates must be able to perform the essential functions of this role with or without reasonable accommodation. Disclaimer: The statements herein are intended to describe the general nature and level of work being performed by the employee in this position. These statements are not intended to be construed as an exhaustive list of all responsibilities, duties, and skills required of a person in this position. Our offices are currently operating in a hybrid model, with staff expected to work in person several days per week. Additional details will be shared if selected for an interview. Salary Information While the majority of new hires’ starting salaries shall be expected to be placed in the first half of the range(s) to allow space to grow in the job, for those who already have significant relevant experience at that level of the job, placement at the higher end of the range(s) is possible. Pay Range $58,009 — $87,012 USD Who We Are For over three decades, New Visions for Public Schools has played a central role in improving the quality of New York City public schools and removing barriers to the success of low-income students and students of color. We provide educators with the tools, resources, and supports to build and continuously improve strong and responsive systems—through investments in curriculum, technology, student planning tools, and innovative college and career preparatory programs. Equal Employment Opportunity Statement New Visions believes that our teams are most effective when they include representation from the diverse communities we serve, as their perspectives are critical to the work we do. Diversity, equity, and inclusion do not determine who gets hired—that is based on qualifications. They ensure that people who have traditionally had less access to opportunities are considered and, once chosen, feel supported and valued as part of our team. New Visions provides a comprehensive and competitive compensation and benefits package in addition to the opportunity to make a significant impact on education reform and in the lives of urban youth.
