The Division of Traffic Operations is seeking a highly organized and proactive Traffic Operations Grants Specialist in the Finance , Contracts and Innovation Unit.  The selected candidate will serve as a lead coordinator for all federal grants with an emphasis on overseeing the critical federal grant for operational support to the Traffic Management Center grant. Reporting to the Deputy Director of Traffic Operations Finance, the Specialist is responsible for managing grant proposals and awards for Traffic Operations including discretionary and formula grants for Traffic Operations initiatives and activities. The Specialist will work with applicable federal and state rules and regulations governing aid to the City. The selected candidate will facilitate the submission of grant applications, management of grant awards, and reimbursement of federal or state funds.  This role offers significant latitude and the opportunity to become the agency’s subject matter expert on federally funded technologies employed by the city for managing transportation systems. The role will focus on the operations of the Traffic Management Center, the central hub for monitoring citywide traffic conditions, managing emergency response, and deploying advanced technologies such as Connected Vehicles and Transit Signal Priority. Grant funding supports engineers in conducting transportation studies and implementing emerging technologies.  About NYC DOT and the Division of Traffic Operations  NYC DOT works to support the safe, equitable, and sustainable movement of people and goods across New York City. Within NYC DOT, the Division of Traffic Operations delivers and sustains the systems that help New Yorkers and visitors move safely and efficiently every day. Traffic Operations manages the operation of more than 350,000 streetlights, approximately 14,000 signalized intersections, roughly 90,000 on-street parking spaces, over 4,000 automated enforcement cameras, and a state-of-the-art Traffic Management Center. These roles will support the expansion and modernization of DOT’s Automated Enforcement program, which consists of red light, speed, and bus lane cameras. Work across the division spans signals and street lighting, traffic management and intelligent transportation systems, parking operations, modeling and data analysis, and automated enforcement much of it delivered through grants and supported through effective grant planning and administration. The Office of Curb Management within the Division of Transportation Planning & Management is responsible for curb policies across the city’s 6,300 miles of streets and roughly 3 million curbside parking spaces, with a focus on improving safety, reducing double parking and better managing competing demands — from loading zones and deliveries to charging infrastructure and waste containerization to support safer, more efficient streets across the city  The Office of Curb Management is seeking a candidate to fill the role of Parking Data Analyst within that unit. In this role, the selected candidate will be charged with developing and implementing a citywide data collection program to examine curbside activity metrics in select neighborhoods throughout the city. This may include overseeing consultant processing of timelapse photos, overseeing spreadsheet/data analysis in Microsoft Excel and similar databases, and ensuring collected data is clean and mappable.  •	Data reporting The candidate will be responsible for writing periodic reports on the status of the data collection effort including annual reports. This will include interpreting the data collection to communicate to a both a technical and general audience, writing reports, generating charts, creating maps, and presenting to DOT leadership.  The candidate should have a solid foundation of experience in transportation planning and data collection of parking and transportation metrics. jobs.title: Planning, Design and Policy Analyst, Public Realm
jobs.description: Transportation Planning and Management (TPM) is responsible for the safe, efficient, and environmentally responsible movement of people and goods on the City's streets, supporting the larger goals of economic and social vitality for people living, working, and doing business in New York City.  The Division’s responsibilities include planning, street design, technical analysis, signs, transit development, freight mobility and markings, ensuring the safety of motor vehicle occupants, pedestrians, and cyclists. The Office Livable Streets (OLS) is tasked with prioritizing strategic planning, community engagement, research, policy, design, implementation, and long-term management. Their goal is to create streets that are livable, supporting safety, accessibility, inclusion, resiliency, active modes, community cohesion, and economic vitality citywide. Additionally, they aim to enhance New York City's pedestrian, bicycle, and micromobility networks, providing comfortable, connected, green, and reliable transportation options across the five boroughs. They place special emphasis on Priority Investment Areas, mode shift, and reimagining streets. The office also develops innovative new programs, design typologies, project delivery, and analysis tools to meet the demands of a rapidly changing population with evolving needs and technologies. The multidisciplinary Public Realm Unit is responsible for engaging New Yorkers to reimagine and utilize their city streets as public space and oversees the development of programs, policies, projects, and management tools to elevate the public realm experience for its primary user – the pedestrian. Through initiatives and programs ranging from the Pedestrian Mobility Plan, Public Space Programming, the Public Space Equity Program, Open Streets, Super Sidewalks, Street Seats, Complex Intersections, Shared Streets and Plazas, the Public Realm Unit creates vibrant and inclusive spaces that improve safety, accessibility, and walkability while enhancing commerce, community, and culture throughout New York City.  OLS is seeking a motivated Planning, Design and Policy Analyst for its Public Realm Unit within the TPM Division. Reporting to the Public Realm’s Director of Strategic Initiatives (SI), the successful candidate will work closely with the SI Director and Transportation Planning and Management teams to produce neighborhood scale planning and transportation studies that promote equity, walkability, mode shift, and opportunities for greening. jobs.title: Application Developer
jobs.description: DCAS's mission is to make city government work for all New Yorkers. DCAS Information Technology works in conjunction with the NYC Office of Technology and Innovation (OTI) on the daily management and support of the DCAS computer network. The candidate selected for this role will be responsible for: supporting, maintaining, and enhancing Centre 360, the City's public reservation platform for the panoramic experience atop the David N. Dinkins Municipal Building. Working as part of a collaborative team and reporting to senior development staff, the Application Developer will resolve technical issues, build out new features, and help ensure the platform remains stable, secure, and performant under public-facing demand. In addition, this candidate may be called upon to provide development support and coverage for other critical citywide systems managed by the DCAS internal team.   As an Application Developer on the Centre 360 team, you will:  • Support the ongoing development, maintenance, and enhancement of Centre 360. • Troubleshoot and resolve technical issues in a timely manner to minimize downtime and impact to the public, including during monthly reservation openings and peak demand periods. • Develop new features and functionality based on business needs and visitor feedback. • Write clean, scalable code and perform code reviews with peers. • Collaborate with senior developers, QA, and business analysts to design, test, and deploy software updates. • Contribute to API development and integration with other City systems and services. • Support the reservation, scheduling, and capacity-management functionality that powers the visitor booking experience. • Participate in data migration, reporting, and dashboard development as needed. • Help ensure system security and compliance with internal IT and OTI standards. • Maintain clear and accurate documentation of system architecture, configuration, and development processes.  Only permanent employees in the civil service title of Computer Specialist (Software), a comparable title, and those that are reachable on the civil service list are eligible to apply. Only those candidates under consideration will be contacted.  This position is also open to qualified persons with a disability who are eligible for the 55-a Program. Please indicate in your cover letter that you would like to be considered for the position under the 55-a Program. Minimum qualifications: (1) A baccalaureate degree from an accredited college, including or supplemented by twenty-four (24) semester credits in computer science or a related computer field and two (2) years of satisfactory full-time software experience in designing, programming, debugging, maintaining, implementing, and enhancing computer software applications, systems programming, systems analysis and design, data communication software, or database design and programming, including one year in a project leader capacity or as a major contributor on a complex project; or  (2) A four-year high school diploma or its educational equivalent and six (6) years of full-time satisfactory software experience as described in “1" above, including one year in a project leader capacity or as a major contributor on a complex project; or  (3) A satisfactory combination of education and experience that is equivalent to (1) or (2) above. College education may be substituted for up to two years of the required experience in (2) above on the basis that sixty (60) semester credits from an accredited college is equated to one year of experience. A masters degree in computer science or a related computer field may be substituted for one year of the required experience in (1) or (2) above. However, all candidates must have a four year high school diploma or its educational equivalent, plus at least one (1) year of satisfactory full-time software experience in a project leader capacity or as a major contributor on a complex project.  NOTE: In order to have your experience accepted as Project Leader or Major Contributor experience, you must explain in detail how your experience qualifies you as a project leader or as a major contributor. Experience in computer operations, technical support, quality assurance (QA), hardware installation, help desk, or as an end user will not be accepted for meeting the minimum qualification  requirements.  Special Note  To be eligible for placement in Assignment Level IV, in addition to the Qualification Requirements stated above, individuals must have one year of satisfactory experience in a project leader capacity or as a major contributor on a complex project in data administration, database management systems, operating systems, data communications systems, capacity planning, and/or on-line applications programming. Preferred skills: The preferred candidate will bring the following skills and experience to this position:  - Agile/Scrum development practices and experience with tools such as Jira or Azure DevOps. - Experience with data integration and ETL processes; familiarity with Azure Data Factory or SSIS. - Experience with AI/ML integration, including Azure OpenAI, Cognitive Services, or similar. - Familiarity with GitHub Copilot or other AI orchestration tools. - Knowledge of NoSQL databases such as Azure Cosmos DB or MongoDB. - C#, ASP.NET Core, JavaScript - HTML, CSS, Bootstrap, Vue.js or React or Angular - Azure cloud services (App Services, Application Insights, Blob Storage) - Experience with Git and Agile/Scrum workflows in Azure DevOps or GitHub - Experience working with RESTful web services - Familiarity with Docker and containerization - Scripting or automation experience (PowerShell, Bash, or Python) - Good writing, communication, and team collaboration skills and requirements gathering - Ability to conduct quality assurance and design performance tests using testing procedures

jobs.title: Policy Advisor, Multifamily Climate Solutions
jobs.description: The Agency You’ll Join:  The New York City Mayor’s Office is responsible for overseeing city services throughout the five boroughs, coordinating public agencies and departments, and managing public property. The administration is leading the fight in making the city more affordable, reducing inequality, improving public safety, ensuring delivery of efficient and effective services, and working to make New York City’s economy stronger. We value leadership, transparency, fairness, and efficiency as we actively seek diverse talents from various sectors to join our team. For current job opportunities, visit our careers page.   The Team You’ll Work With:  The Mayor’s Office of Climate and Environmental Justice (MOCEJ) is a team of architects, lawyers, data and climate scientists, engineers, policy advisors, geologists, and city planners working to create a city where our 8.8 million New Yorkers can live, work, learn, and play in healthy, resilient, and sustainable neighborhoods. MOCEJ integrates sustainability, resiliency, and environmental justice into one coordinated approach across several climate and environmental offices, all working to make our buildings efficient and resilient; our infrastructure climate-ready; our streets, open spaces, and public realm active, safe, and healthy; and our energy clean and resilient. All New Yorkers deserve safe, healthy, resilient, and sustainable environments, even as the climate changes.  MOCEJ is committed to improving environmental quality for all, prioritizing front-line communities, seeking to redress current and past injustices and inequities while creating economic opportunities for all. Through science-based analysis, policy and program development, and capacity building, MOCEJ leads the City’s efforts to ensure that New York City is minimizing its contributions to climate change, preparing to adapt and protect New Yorkers from extreme weather and multiple climate hazards, and giving every New Yorker a meaningful voice in our city’s future.   The Problems You’ll Solve:   As the Policy Advisor for the Multifamily Housing Climate Solutions, you will support MOCEJ’s efforts to accelerate building decarbonization and resiliency across New York City’s multifamily housing stock. Reporting to the Director for Sustainable Buildings, you will advance program delivery, engage with stakeholders, and support policy development to advance Local Law 97 compliance and building sustainability requirements.    Program Implementation    •	Support implementation and operations of a citywide Co-op Solutions Hub within the NYC Accelerator program to advance multifamily building compliance with Local Law 97 and other local building sustainability laws.    •	Provide general support across the NYC Accelerator program with a focus on multifamily buildings.   •	Lead and coordinate workshops with the NYC Accelerator team, via organizing cohorts of similar multifamily buildings such as cooperative housing, condominiums, and affordable housing.   •	Identify barriers to decarbonization in multifamily buildings and opportunities to overcome them.   Stakeholder Engagement and Interagency Coordination   •	Act as a point of contact for cooperative housing boards and facilitate connections to city and state administrators to streamline LL97 compliance and other administrative processes.   •	Support coordination and collaboration with partner agencies, community-based organizations, and advocacy groups, as well as with The Council of New York Cooperatives & Condominiums.   •	Attend co-op, condo, and multifamily-related events, expos, and meetings to promote the Co-op Hub and learn about trends and innovation in the industry.   •	Represent MOCEJ at meetings, community forums, conferences, and other events.  Policy Research and Data Analysis   •	Research policy initiatives, funding opportunities, and process improvements to support building system modernization and decarbonization in multifamily housing, including but not limited to resources, technical assistance, and program design for grants, rebates, and incentives.   •	Analyze large and complex data sets related to building information, local demographics, environmental justice indicators, retrofit and energy costs, energy use, and GHG emissions to identify gaps, trends, anomalies, and opportunities.   •	Write, review, and edit key policy reports and publications.   •	Track and evaluate policies, initiatives, incentives, and legislation at the City, State, and Federal levels that support multifamily building decarbonization.   About You:  •	You have exceptional organizational skills and attention to detail, including the ability to manage complex projects, coordinate multi-stakeholder programs, and maintain control of analytical  details while balancing overarching program objectives within a fast-paced, high-stakes environment.   •	You have strong interpersonal and collaboration skills, with the ability to build effective relationships with internal and external stakeholders, particularly with community-based organizations, housing advocacy groups, and co-operative housing industry associations.  •	You have excellent communication skills, especially communicating complex issues to audiences with varying levels of technical understanding.  •	You have strong working knowledge of New York City’s building sustainability landscape, including Local Law 97, and the ability to translate complex policy requirements into actionable steps for non-technical audiences.   •	You have a strong understanding of New York state, and federal regulations and policies on multifamily buildings, particularly those related to GHG emissions reduction, building energy performance standards, climate change, environmental justice, and resiliency.   •	You have demonstrated experience in program implementation or project management, specifically in launching new operational frameworks or multi-stakeholder outreach initiatives.   •	You have knowledge of building systems and technology, with a focus on energy efficiency, decarbonization, and electrification projects in multifamily housing.   •	You have an understanding of local cooperative housing governance structures and decision-making processes.   •	You are proficient in using Microsoft Excel and related tools to conduct analysis of large and complex data sets.   •	You are familiar with financial incentive structures and special purpose entities, including the ability to research and identify new and existing grants, rebates, tax incentives, and low-interest financing tools for multifamily building retrofits. Minimum qualifications: 1. A baccalaureate degree and two (2) years of responsible full-time paid experience in one or more of the fields of: information technology, methods analysis, operations research, systems analysis, financial administration, cost effectiveness, or fiscal and economic program or design evaluation; or    2. A satisfactory equivalent of education and experience.  However, all candidates must possess at least one year of the experience as described under “1”. Preferred skills: •	A baccalaureate or master’s degree from an accredited college or university in Urban Planning, Public Policy, Sustainability, Real Estate, Architecture, Construction Management, Energy Management, Environmental Policy, Facilities Management, or a closely related field.   •	3–5 years of experience working in building decarbonization, housing finance, stakeholder engagement, community organizing, or property management, with a specific focus on NYC multifamily buildings (affordable housing, co-ops, condos, or Mitchell-Lama developments).   •	You have liaison and advocacy skills to work effectively across government agencies while advocating for new resources or programmatic improvements.   •	You can manage and analyze large data sets to identify trends, anomalies, and develop top-line insights and takeaways for internal and external talking points and presentations.

The Research & Planning Coordinator supports the integration of scientific findings into stream management practices, program planning, flood hazard mitigation, watershed protection, and ecological restoration efforts. DEP’s SMP works with local, regional, and state partners to protect and restore stream system stability and ecological integrity through long-term stewardship of streams and floodplains. The SMP develops and implements stream management strategies that reduce flood and erosion hazards, protect infrastructure and water quality, and improve aquatic and riparian habitat conditions.  -Assist with procurement, administration, and management of contracts, task orders, cooperative agreements, and technical service agreements, including monitoring budgets, processing payments, and workshops, and interagency collaboration related to stream management, watershed resilience, flood mitigation, and environmental planning initiatives.  -Prepare management reports, technical monitoring, post-flood evaluations, field investigations, and scientific data collection efforts, as needed, to support SMP objectives and program implementation.  -Provide technical support and recommendations to DEP leadership, SMP partners, and stakeholders regarding watershed management, stream restoration, climate resilience, flood hazard mitigation, environmental planning, and related scientific or technical initiatives, and perform related work as assigned. jobs.description: The Center for Health Equity & Community Wellness (CHECW) seeks to eliminate inequities resulting in premature mortality. With an unwavering grounding in history and structural analysis, CHECW works to increase visibility of socially unjust policy while pushing towards redress for the most impacted NYC communities. CHECW addresses inequity across community and healthcare systems in partnership with community, faith-based, and health care organizations. CHECW's work focuses on social determinants of health, including environmental and commercial determinants, and addresses both upstream and downstream factors to improve health and well-being of New Yorkers. CHECW is comprised of the Bureau of Bronx Neighborhood Health, the Bureau of Brooklyn Neighborhood Health, the Bureau of Harlem Neighborhood Health, the Bureau of Chronic Disease Prevention, the Bureau of Health Equity Capacity Building, the Bureau of Equitable Health Systems and the Bureau of Finance, Administration and Services. The Division's Deputy Commissioner also serves as the Agency's Chief Equity Officer and oversees Race to Justice, the Agency's internal reform effort to help our staff learn what they can do to better address racial health gaps and improve health outcomes for all New Yorkers. The division's Deputy Commissioner also serves as the Agency's Chief Medical Officer. The Bureau of Bronx Neighborhood works with clinical and community partners to expand access to high-quality, culturally responsive programs that prevent and manage chronic diseases, especially for residents facing the greatest health challenges. The Bureau provides public health and social services, coordinates community events, builds collaborative partnerships, and leads research and evaluation initiatives that drive evidence-based action, close health gaps and advance equity across the Bronx. From diabetes and asthma education to nutrition, food security, newborn safety, and childbirth classes, the Bureau empowers New Yorkers with the knowledge and tools to live healthier lives. jobs.title: Data Governance & Special Projects Coordinator, Bureau of Vital Statistics
jobs.description: The Center for Population Health Data Science (CPHDS) within the NYC Department of Health and Mental Hygiene (DOHMH) aims to catalyze critical data modernization work by linking public health, healthcare, and social service data. The Center works to make these data more accessible, timely, equitable, meaningfully usable, and protected – and actively used to protect and promote the health and wellbeing of New Yorkers. The Bureau of Vital Statistics (BVS) is responsible for registering and certifying al birth, deaths, and spontaneous terminations of pregnancy in NYC. The Bureau issues, analyzes, and reports on 285,000 vital events each year. The Bureau is a very large customer service operation, providing death certification services on a 24/7 basis, issuing more than 900,000 certified copies of birth and death records, and fulfilling hundreds of data requests annually. Project Management & Coordination  - Lead and manage special projects as assigned by OVS leadership.  - Attend meetings and events on behalf of OVS leadership.  - Organize meetings, prepare agendas, take minutes, assign follow-ups, and monitor action items.  - Track publication outputs, performance measures, and historical data requests for OVS, as pertains to data requests, sharing, and collaborations.  - Contribute to enhancing OVS systems for project management and tracking. CYF-DD relies on research and surveillance to guide its decisions around policy development, service planning, implementation and evaluation and incorporates a health equity lens into its work. CYF-DD oversees a portfolio of over 100 programs and supports a family-driven, individualized and strength-based approach to care. jobs.title: Drug-Checking Data Analyst, Bureau of Alcohol and Drug Use
jobs.description: The Bureau of Alcohol and Drug Use (BADU) works to close gaps and reduce overall morbidity and mortality related to alcohol and substance use among New Yorkers. BADU develops, implements, and evaluates interventions and prevention strategies through contracting of treatment, recovery and support services; policy analysis and development; epidemiology and surveillance; dissemination of treatment and management guidelines; harm reduction initiatives; public and provider outreach and education; and community involvement and interagency collaboration. The Bureau amplifies the voices of those most impacted and focuses on inequitable structural, social, service, and communication factors that drive disparities. The Office of Research, Surveillance, Policy, and Communications within BADU conducts alcohol- and drug-related surveillance, program evaluation and research, maintains databases, designs research protocols, produces reports, writes scientific articles for peer-reviewed journals, facilitates program and policy development, and develops messaging and other communication materials for provider and public audiences. In 2021, BADU established a drug-checking pilot to gain more insight into the unregulated drug supply and provide fact based information to people using the service. Using Fourier-transform infrared spectroscopy (FTIR) and immunoassay test strips, trained drug checking technicians currently offer point-of-care drug-checking services at syringe service program locations in Manhattan, the Bronx, and Brooklyn, including two sites that offer overdose prevention services.   The Drug-Checking Data Analyst will support the development and implementation of data collection, analysis, and reporting systems for the drug-checking initiative. The Drug-Checking Data Analyst work collaboratively with the Drug Checking Team to coordinate and support data management activities, including monitoring and analyzing program data, ensuring data quality, supporting data requests, and preparing data products for internal and external stakeholders.  DUTIES WILL INCLUDE BUT NOT BE LIMITED TO: 1. Extract, clean, manipulate, organize, and analyze drug-checking data primarily using R, REDCap, Excel, SQL, and other platforms 2. Work collaboratively with drug-checking technicians to perform quality assurance data checks and implement quality improvement processes to ensure data quality 3. Support the Senior Drug Checking Epidemiologist in designing and developing new methods of analyses for the drug-checking initiative in conjunction with the Bureau’s drug-related syndromic surveillance data to inform future program direction 4. Contribute to the design and maintenance of the drug-checking database, including queries and data entry procedures and preparing documentation 5. Support the creation and revision of study and data management documentation related to the drug-checking program, including data dictionaries and codebooks 6. Assist with the reporting of programmatic data, including, but not limited to, internal reporting (e.g., weekly reports, dashboards), external reporting, Power Point presentations, and ad-hoc data requests 7. Support the maintenance of a drug-checking dashboard and other data visualization activities 8. Assist with development of protocols, workflows, questionnaires, and surveys 9. Support the preparation of IRB applications for research study protocols 10. Contribute to the development of manuscripts for peer-reviewed journals 11. Contribute to the Bureau’s racial justice and health equity activities  PREFERRED SKILLS: • Experience practicing public health and working across systems to further a public health approach to substance use • Experience with program monitoring, evaluation, and/or quality improvement • Knowledge of and experience within the fields of substance use/harm reduction • Experience (at least 1 year) analyzing public health data in an applied setting using R • Experience with quantitative data, including the ability to read, interpret and synthesize epidemiologic and other scientific literature • Experience with survey data collection and database management using REDCap, SQL, Microsoft Access or similar platforms • Experience with or willingness to learn data visualization and dashboarding tools (e.g., Power BI, Tableau) • Able to work independently and as part of a team • Exceptional interpersonal, research, written, and verbal communication skills • Excellent organizational skills and attention to detail • Proficiency in Excel, Access, Word, and PowerPoint • Able to multitask in a fast-faced, high-volume environment • Passionate about implementing interventions and conducting analyses with the end goal of reducing drug-related morbidity and mortality in New York City  Why you should work for us:  - Loan Forgiveness: As a prospective employee of the City of New York, you may be eligible for federal/state loan forgiveness and repayment assistance programs that lessen your payments or even fully forgive your full balance. jobs.description: Since its creation as the Board of Health in 1805, DOHMH has set the national standard for public health. DOHMH has been a leader in utilizing community-level survey and epidemiologic data, cutting-edge information technology, and evidence-based and evidence-informed practices to prioritize and address the health issues of ultimate importance to NYC’s 8.4 million residents. DOHMH balances its role of protecting and promoting the health of all New Yorkers with the rights of those individuals to determine their own health-related behaviors. It achieves this balance by investing in public health interventions that work with communities to change the environmental context, making healthy options the default choice, regardless of education, income, and socioeconomic status. Within DOHMH, the Division of Family and Child Health (FCH) works to improve the health of children, women, and families in New York City, with an emphasis on reducing health disparities and advancing equity. The Division’s diverse and expansive portfolio of work ranges from providing home visits to new parents, to caring for acute and chronic conditions in school children, to engaging communities around promoting sexual and reproductive justice. Four bureaus comprise the Division: Bureau of Maternal, Infant and Reproductive Health, Bureau of Early Intervention, Office of School Health, and Bureau of Administration. We encourage qualified applicants with demonstrated commitment to social justice, particularly racial, gender, and LGBTQ equity to apply. We share data and research findings to encourage evidence-based decision making, and partner with communities in community science and outreach to address stakeholder concerns and empower residents.   The GIS Analyst supports field data collection for programs across the Division of Environmental Health including building and maintaining tools such as ESRI’s Survey123 and Field Maps for inspectional staff in the Bureau of Food Safety and other bureaus. jobs.title: Health Product Development & Engineering Lead, Bureau of Data Technology & Strategy
jobs.description: The Center for Population Health Data Science (CPHDS)- launched in October of 2023- aims to catalyze critical data modernization work and enable the agency to make progress toward linking public health, healthcare, and social service for timely and effective publication. We are working towards making these data more accessible, timely, equitable, meaningfully usable, and protected – and actively used to protect and promote the health and wellbeing of New Yorkers. We aim to strengthen agencywide data capabilities by empowering our workforce, enhancing intra- and inter-agency data sharing, and using modern technology to yield trusted and integrated data and insights. A real-time and comprehensive view of city needs is needed to enhance public health actions and improve health outcomes for the most vulnerable New Yorkers. The CPHDS is working to strengthen citywide population health surveillance by better linking public health, healthcare, and social service data to fully characterize and improve the health of New Yorkers. Our vision is for these data to be accessible, timely, equitable, meaningfully usable, and protected in order to protect and promote health and wellbeing of New Yorkers. The Bureau of Data Technology and Strategy (DTS) is home to data strategy, data communication, data governance, data product management, data engineering, and data science capabilities. The Unified Data Experience (UDX) team is working to modernize how the agency communicates data to the public, ensuring usability, accessibility, and approachability of al public-facing data communication products.  DUTIES WILL INCLUDE BUT NOT BE LIMITED TO: • Lead the engineering and development of the UDX platform: choosing technologies, architectures, and componentry to support development and desired workflows. • Collaborate with team on research and design – turning internal and external needs into prototypes and prototypes into product. • Identify design or technical problems and devise elegant, timely, and cost-effective solutions. • Lead and guide other contributors including junior developers and UX designers. • Communicate design, development, and technical decisions and trade-o fs to internal stakeholders. • Ask insightful questions, take risks, and champion innovative ideas that facilitate the use of data for action. jobs.description: The Center for Health Equity and Community Wellness (CHECW) seeks to eliminate racial and other inequities resulting in premature mortality.  With an unwavering grounding in history and structural analysis, CHECW addresses inequity across community and healthcare systems in partnership with community, faith-based, and health care organizations. The Bureau of Equitable Health Systems (BEHS) is the health care systems bureau of DOHMH. Our mission is to apply policy, evidence, and practical expertise to improve equity in health care delivery at the individual, organizational and systems levels. The Health Care Access & Policy (HCAP) Office within BEHS drives policy, programming, and research that maximizes health insurance coverage and increases access to a fordable high quality, and coordinated primary care with a strong focus on health equity. HCAP has dedicated staff working to improve access to quality, culturally appropriate primary care for New Yorkers, particularly those who are at risk for poor health outcome, by ensuring that on-the ground programmatic work, policy, and data activities inform one another. Within HCAP sits the Healthy Aging Unit, a program that builds support for older adults and their caregivers and strengthens the NYC Health Department's ability to monitor and respond to the health needs of older adults. The unit offers an exciting, unique opportunity for a public health professional with an interest in disease prevention, healthcare policy, health insurance (Medicare/Medicaid), and research.   The Bureau of Equitable Health Systems seeks to hire a Healthy Aging Program Coordinator who must be able to effectively manage initiatives and multiple projects simultaneously in supporting the Bureau's mission.  DUTIES WILL INCLUDE BUT NOT BE LIMITED TO: - Contribute to strategizing, developing, implementing, and evaluating program initiatives that help support the health of older adults and address intersectional inequities.  - Assist in research and quantitative data analysis on public health initiatives including health insurance and including reviewing relevant literature.  - Disseminate information and serve as liaison between the Healthy Aging Unit and other agency programs and assist with troubleshooting.  - Coordinate with other city agencies to align priorities related to Healthy Aging.  - Collaborate with policy-focused staff across the agency to analyze and interpret aging-related policies and policies related to health insurance for older adults.  - Coordinate communication efforts to internal and external partners.  - Prepare reports, as appropriate.  - Conduct background research and prepare proposals for new programs.  - Maintain up-to-date knowledge base on relevant policy issues including public health insurance programs, health reform and transformation initiatives impacting primary care and health insurance coverage and healthy aging.  - Assist in planning, coordinating, and evaluating educational events, community outreach activities, and Healthy Aging initiatives.  - Maintain and update Healthy Aging contact lists, partner networks, and program resources.  - Identify and coordinate community outreach opportunities and events to support NYC Health Department engagement with older adults. jobs.title: Manager for Translational Epidemiology, World Trade Center Health Registry
jobs.description: The World Trade Center Health Registry (WTCHR) was created in 2002 to monitor and evaluate the physical and mental health impact on more than 71,000 persons exposed to the September 11, 2001 disaster. Housed within the Center for Population Health Data Science in a renowned and dynamic agency, WTCHR research influences national policies concerning healthcare for those who survived the attacks and contributes novel epidemiologic findings to the post-disaster public health literature. Reporting to the Director of Research, you will be serving as the manager for a newly established sub-unit devoted to Translational Epidemiology. As manager for the Translational Epidemiology sub-unit, you will oversee and improve effectiveness and reach of our Treatment Referral Program, design and integrate multi-source data pipelines for detection of 9/11-related emerging conditions, and serve as a resource for advanced predictive analytics. jobs.title: Naloxone Informatics Specialist, Bureau of Alcohol and Drug Use
jobs.description: The Bureau of Alcohol and Drug Use Prevention, Care, and Treatment (BADUPCT) works to close gaps and reduce overall morbidity and mortality related to alcohol and substance use among New Yorkers. BADUPCT develops, implements, and evaluates interventions and prevention strategies through contracting of treatment, recovery and support services; policy analysis and development; epidemiology and surveillance; dissemination of treatment and management guidelines; harm reduction initiatives; public and provider outreach and education; and community involvement and interagency collaboration. The Bureau amplifies the voices of those most impacted and focuses on inequitable structural, social, service, and communication factors that drive disparities.  The Overdose Education and Naloxone Distribution Unit (OENDU) develops, implements, and evaluates initiatives to reduce and prevent opioid overdose deaths in New York City. The Unit provides naloxone, training, and technical assistance to over 350 Opioid Overdose Prevention Programs (OOPPs) across New York City. OOPPs provide community-based overdose prevention, recognition, and response education and distribute naloxone directly to community members. OENDU solicits data from these OOPPs to evaluate their naloxone dispensing. DOHMH has its own OOPP and provides in-person and virtual overdose prevention training and naloxone via mail-based distribution. In addition, OENDU provides contract management, fiscal, technical, and programmatic support to at least 27 contracted OOPPs for strategic naloxone distribution and 4 contracted OOPPs for the implementation and management of 8 Public Health Vending Machines.   Position Summary:    The Naloxone Informatics Specialist will support the Overdose Prevention Unit by supporting the submission of accurate and timely naloxone distribution data, with the goal of preventing overdose deaths in New York City.  Under general direction from the Naloxone Data Coordinator, with wide latitude for independent judgment and initiative, the Naloxone Informatics Specialist will:  Job Duties and Responsibilities:    •	Collaborate with colleagues in OENDU and the Bureau of Alcohol and Drug Use (BADU) to gather and analyze data related to naloxone dispensing and distribution in NYC  •	Use Microsoft Access and/or R studio to clean and maintain data related to naloxone dispensing and distribution initiatives in NYC  •	Generate PowerBI dashboards and data tables to support the ongoing evaluation of naloxone dispensing and distribution initiatives in NYC.  •	Solicit monthly naloxone distribution reports from over 190 Opioid Overdose Prevention Programs (OOPPs); follow up with OOPPs who do not submit timely reports and provide technical assistance as needed  •	Train newly registered OOPPs to submit individual-level dispensing data through the Naloxone Dispensing Form (NDF); support OOPPs as they integrate form submission into their workflows; monitor form submission and provide support to OOPPs to increase their response rate.   •	Manage timely entry of monthly distribution reports into database; reconcile naloxone fulfillment with monthly data; manage timely preparation of report materials for data processing  •	Develop and refine surveys, RedCap forms, and other dispensing data collection forms as needed.  •	Collaborate with NYS Department of Health AIDS Institute, the Overdose Prevention Coordinator, the Naloxone Inventory Coordinator, and other BADUPCT staff to maintain registration and contact information for all OOPPs  •	Provide timely response to requests for naloxone fulfillment and dispensing data, naloxone reversals and other relevant information  •	Refine systems, as needed, for tracking naloxone dispensing data   •	Support Naloxone Inventory Coordinator in the packaging of naloxone kits  •	Participate in Overdose Prevention Unit meetings, including facilitation on a rotating basis; provide administrative support to the Overdose Prevention Unit including scheduling meetings, developing agendas, and other tasks as needed.  •	Participate in agency-wide activities for advancing racial, gender, and social equity.  •	Other duties or tasks may be assigned on an as-needed basis  Preferred Skills:   •	Knowledge of substance use issues and harm reduction practice and theory, including syringe exchange, overdose prevention and education for HIV and Hepatitis C prevention. •	Experience with quantitative data, including the ability to read, interpret and synthesize epidemiologic and other scientific literature. •	Ability to work independently and as part of a team. Possess exceptional interpersonal, research, written and verbal communication skills.  •	The candidate will also be detail-oriented with outstanding organizational skills.  •	Ability to multi-task in a fast-paced, high volume environment.  •	Proficiency in Excel, Access, Word, and PowerPoint. •	Experience querying or managing data using code, such as SQL, SAS, or R. jobs.title: Policy Manager, Bureau of Children, Youth, Families & Development Disabilities
jobs.description: The Bureau of Children, Youth, Families & Developmental Disabilities (CYF-DD) is responsible for planning and monitoring much of NYC's comprehensive network of child and adolescent community mental health services. Grounded in a commitment to equity, the CYF-DD's mission is to promote the mental health of all children, youth and families and to empower individuals with developmental disabilities to lead integrated and fulfilling lives. To achieve this, we work to improve policies, plan and fund services, conduct research and evaluation, support community based partners and connect children and youth to needed services. CYF-DD's Office of Policy and Planning supports the bureau’s mission by understanding community needs, conducting mental health and intellectual/developmental disabilities systems-level planning, shaping effective policy changes, and ensuring that program models and initiatives are fiscally viable and responsive to need.  DUTIES WILL INCLUDE BUT NOT BE LIMITED TO: • Lead the development of the bureau’s policy agenda by identifying opportunities for policy advancement to improve outcomes for children, youth, and families and people with IDD. • Conduct prompt research and analysis of local, state and national policies including: legislation, regulations, guidance, budgets, and emerging trends. • Research and analyze current and future reimbursement and payment systems to improve access to care (e.g. Medicaid, VBP, managed care, etc.). • Write and present research findings and policy recommendations, including via briefs, memos, literature reviews, presentations, and reports, to advise office and bureau leadership on bureau policy priorities and action. • Help bureau staff to build knowledge of relevant policy issues and the policy development process. • Monitor emerging legislative, regulatory and other policy proposals related to the mental and emotional wellbeing of children, youth, and families and people with IDD, including those involved in multiple child-serving systems, and coordinate the development of bureau comments on these proposals by developing summaries, and drafting comments. • Maintain a database to track and document local, state, and federal policy issues and the bureau’s efforts to advance policy priorities. • Assist with the design and implementation of quantitative and qualitative data collection (e.g. surveys, focus groups, informational interviews), in collaboration with the Office of Research and Evaluation and interpret and apply population-level data for policy development (e.g. Medicaid). • Develops and maintains relationships with government partners and other stakeholders. • Support the development of the bureau’s planning agenda, including the development of the local government service plan. • Support the bureau’s licensing application review team with policy summaries and analysis. • Incorporate racial equity and social justice principles to ensure that priorities and recommendations are aimed at eliminating structural racism and racial inequalities. • Supervise policy analyst staff in the Office of Policy and jobs.title: Program Coordinator, Bureau of Division Management & Systems Coordination
jobs.description: The Division of Disease Control’s mission is to safeguard the health of New Yorkers through identification, surveillance, treatment, control, and prevention of infectious diseases, which is achieved through varied and interrelated endeavors of its seven Bureaus. The Bureau of Division Management & Systems Coordination (DMSC) leads administrative, surveillance, informatics, preparedness, policy, communications, community engagement, and racial equity and social justice activities for the Division and guides the strategic use of Division resources to advance innovative and effective policies and programs.   We are seeking to fill a position in the Division of Disease Control that will provide key support for grant coordination and sustainability initiatives. It is expected that the position will work 35 hours per week to help coordinate grant related activities, track progress on grant milestones, support cross-bureau programmatic coordination, and assist with sustainability initiatives and other projects. This position will work across teams and bureaus to ensure timely reporting and alignment with organizational goals and will report to the Director, Programs and Strategy within DMSC.  DUTIES WILL INCLUDE BUT NOT BE LIMITED TO: • Collaborate with internal teams and bureaus to plan, monitor, and evaluate grant funded public health initiatives, ensuring milestones and deliverables align with federal program requirements and Division goals. • Develop and maintain systems to analyze program performance and fiscal progress, ensuring compliance with grant requirements and supporting scientific and programmatic decision making. • Prepare and submit analytic, fiscal, and programmatic reports that synthesize data from federally funded public health programs and support Division level planning and research. • Support long term program planning and sustainability strategy development for grant funded public health initiatives, incorporating data analysis and program evaluation findings. • Identify opportunities to align grant deliverables, fiscal resources, and program strategies and performance measurements with organizational sustainability and public health infrastructure modernization objectives. • Assist in developing program plans, evaluation and research frameworks, and fiscal analyses that guide long term impact and sustainability of major federally funded initiatives, including Division wide infectious disease prevention programs. • Contribute to the preparation of scientifically and programmatically aligned grant proposals, renewals, and amendments, incorporating program evaluation findings. • Coordinate cross divisional evaluation efforts as needed, including structured assessment of program data (e.g., Mentorship Program), and prepare analytic summaries that inform program planning. • Coordinate scientific, evaluative, and programmatic activities for special bureau programs, ensuring alignment with Division research priorities and grant funded public health initiatives. • Other duties as assigned. To achieve this the Bureau provides direct clinic services to people seeking sexual health care, and services to sex partners; monitors disease trends; provides education and training to providers and community groups, conducts research and develop policies to improve sexual health and wellness. The BPHC STI operates 8 Sexual Health Clinics throughout New York City (NYC). The BPHC STI is requesting to hire a City Research Scientist, L3/Program Implementation Lead who will report directly to Senior Director of Programs. jobs.title: Program Manager, Bureau of Chronic Disease Prevention
jobs.description: The Center for Health Equity & Community Wellness (CHECW) seeks to eliminate racial and other inequities resulting in premature mortality.  With an unwavering grounding in history and structural analysis, CHECW works to increase visibility of the harm perpetuated by centuries of racist, socially unjust policy while pushing towards redress for the most impacted NYC communities. CHECW addresses inequity across community and healthcare systems in partnership with community, faith-based, and health care organizations. CHECW's work focuses on social determinants of health, including environmental and commercial determinants, and addresses both upstream and downstream factors to improve health and well-being of New Yorker. CHECW is comprised of the Bureau of Bronx Neighborhood Health, the Bureau of Brooklyn Neighborhood Health, the Bureau of Harlem Neighborhood Health, the Bureau of Queens Neighborhood Health, the Bureau of Chronic Disease Prevention, the Bureau of Equitable Health Systems and the Bureau of Finance, Administration and Services. The division's Deputy Commissioner also serves as the Agency's Chief Equity Officer and oversees Race To Justice, the Agency's internal reform effort to help our staff learn what they can do to better address racial health gaps and improve health outcomes for all New Yorkers. The NYC Health Department's Bureau of Chronic Disease Prevention (BDCP) strives to reduce the burden of chronic disease, including heart disease, diabetes, and cancer, among New Yorkers. BCDP focuses on nutrition, tobacco use, the built environment, and reducing the impact of cancer. BCDP aims to advance evidence-based policies, programs, community engagement, and research aimed at shifting environments, changing systems and promoting health equity. As a bureau within the NYC Health Department's Center for Health Equity & Community Wellness (CHECW), BCDP contributes to CHECW's goal of eliminating racial inequities and reducing overall premature mortality among New Yorkers. BCDP puts a focus on reducing exposure to and consumption of unhealthy foods and tobacco industry products and countering industry practices that negatively impact health. In addition to pursuing population-level approaches, BCDP prioritizes communities that bear a disproportionate burden of chronic disease.   The Active Design Unit within BCDP seeks to hire a Program Manager, the Program Manager will oversee the implementation and day to day management of the unit's place-based programs in schools and neighborhood settings, including program planning, partnership coordination, research, and evaluation activities. strategic relationships with peer city agencies, community organizations, academic institutions, and other external partners to share information, coordinate activities, and collaborate on projects that support and inform the work of the Active Design Unit.  • Support community engagement and partner coordination throughout program planning and implementation, including activities that incorporate community perspectives and lived experience into Active Design projects.  • Prepare program updates, grant proposals, funder progress reports, and other written materials to communicate program activities, accomplishments, and outcomes.  • Supervise and manage staff and other team members as assigned, providing guidance, setting priorities, and overseeing work assignments.  • Conduct research and review public health and built environment literature to inform the design and implementation of evidence-informed initiatives that leverage urban planning, architecture, and design strategies to promote healthy behaviors and improve health outcomes.  • Coordinate with Bureau and agency colleagues and external city agency and private partners to plan and implement research and evaluation activities in support of Active Design programs and strategic initiatives.  • Support the development and implementation of data collection and evaluation protocols to document program implementation, participation, utilization, and outcomes, and contribute to analyses, reports, presentations, and peer-reviewed publications. • Monitor and synthesize emerging research, best practices, and public policy developments related to the built environment, physical activity, mental health, social connection, and other health outcomes, particularly in school and neighborhood se tings.  • Plan and coordinate meetings and events, including developing event logistics, preparing presentations and other materials, and communicating program information to key audiences.  • jobs.title: Program Quality Manager, Bureau of Hepatitis, HIV, and STI
jobs.description: The NYC Health Department’s Bureau of Hepatitis, HIV, and Sexually Transmitted Infections (BHHS) falls within the Division of Disease Control, oversees the City's response to viral hepatitis, HIV, and sexually transmitted infections (STIs). Its mission is to improve the lives of New Yorkers by ending transmission, illness, stigma, and inequities related to viral hepatitis, HIV, and STIs. BHHS does this through testing initiatives; prevention, care, and treatment programming; epidemiology and surveillance; training and technical assistance; community engagement; social marketing; policy advocacy; and racial equity and social justice initiatives. BHHS’s over 500 staff members work across eight programs: Administration, HIV Care and Treatment, HIV Epidemiology, HIV Prevention, Policy and External Affairs, Racial Equity and Social Justice Initiatives, STI, and Viral Hepatitis. The Viral Hepatitis Program conducts surveillance, and develops and implements programs and projects to prevent, manage and treat hepatitis B and C in New York City.   Reporting to the Project Director and working with the Capacity Building unit, you will be assigned specific viral hepatitis linkage to care initiatives and strategies addressing the Plan to Eliminate Viral Hepatitis in New York City by 2030. Under direction of the Project Director and Director of Capacity Building, you will develop, implement, and evaluate program activities; meeting with external organization staff (such as program managers, clinicians, and service providers) to understand their program implementation and service delivery needs; and provide tailored technical assistance to support effective program outcomes.  DUTIES WILL INCLUDE BUT NOT BE LIMITED TO: • Monitor contracts and budgets ensuring timely and accurate invoicing in compliance with agency policies and procedures. • Plan and coordinate with contractors the implementation of linkage to care initiatives program model and evidence-based practices (using Salesforce, MS Teams and Planner. • Analyze program data and conduct quality assurance (using REDCap, SAS, Tableau, MS Forms). • Engage collaboratively with internal and external stakeholders to address service delivery needs and improve program outcomes. • Develop, implement and evaluate quality improvement projects to increase viral hepatitis screening, linkage to care, and treatment rates. • Conduct comprehensive literature reviews and critically evaluate health research studies to support implementation of evidence-based strategies and interventions. • Stay up to date on the latest trends, developments and innovations related to viral hepatitis screening, linkage to care, treatment and relevant topics such as immigration and substance use to enhance overall effectiveness of the program. • Contribute to the development and dissemination of program protocols, resources and tools to support program outcomes. • Maintain accurate records and prepare reports. • Support the dissemination of program findings, including for presentations and manuscripts. • Supervise one or two staff. • Contribute to Capacity Building and Viral Hepatitis Program activities. • Contribute to the Bureau’s racial justice and health equity activities. • Complete other tasks as assigned.  PREFERRED SKILLS: • Master’s degree from an accredited college or university with a specialization in public health, health management, or a related field • Strong working knowledge of Salesforce, REDCap SAS, Tableau, Excel and other MS Office software • Experience and expertise in collecting, managing, cleaning, analyzing, and reporting data • Experience in project management, including planning, implementation, and evaluation activities • Ability to coordinate, engage, and foster collaboration among diverse stakeholders, including community organizations, and health care providers • Knowledge of implementation science and public health interventions • Strong written and oral communication skills • Ability to work both independently and within a team • Adaptability and willingness to learn • Ability to prioritize and manage multiple tasks • Professionalism and reliability • Initiative and proactive approach to work • Knowledge of hepatitis B and C, including prevention, control strategies, and current epidemiological trends, as well as broader infectious disease expertise (preferred but not required). jobs.title: Research Scientist for Disaster Epidemiology, World Trade Center Health Registry
jobs.description: The World Trade Center Health Registry (WTCHR) was created in 2002 to monitor and evaluate the physical and mental health impact on more than 71,000 persons exposed to the September 11, 2001 disaster. Housed within the Center for Population Health Data Science in a renowned and dynamic agency, WTCHR research influences national policies concerning healthcare for those who survived the attacks and contributes novel epidemiologic findings to the post-disaster public health literature.    Duties will include but not be limited to:  - Serve as lead epidemiologist for COVID-19-related research and co-investigator for cross-bureau special projects related to COVID-19. - Propose scientific studies in areas of the long-term mental and physical health effects associated with multiple disaster exposure. - Serve as lead author and co-author on manuscript teams that incorporate mentoring junior scientists. - Oversee day-to-day administrative tasks associated with manuscript development and nested study implementation, including cross unit and bureau coordination, developing timelines, staff allocation, budgeting, vendor contracts and negotiation, and IRB. - Oversee external research partnerships/collaborations during the conduct of assigned projects. - Conduct independent analyses of WTCHR data, including employing methods designed to handle longitudinal or hierarchical data and data obtained through administrative linkages, time to event data, and methods common in epidemiology for addressing limitations of longitudinal cohort studies (e.g., missing data, attrition). - Supervise directly or indirectly CRS I, CRS II, and interns, as requested. jobs.title: Research and Evaluation Analyst, Bureau of Epidemiology Services

We aim to strengthen agencywide data capabilities by empowering our workforce, enhancing intra- and inter-agency data sharing, and using modern technology to yield trusted and integrated data and insights. A comprehensive view of city needs is needed to enhance public health action and improve health outcomes for the most vulnerable New Yorkers. The CPHDS is working to strengthen citywide population health surveillance by be ter linking public health, healthcare, and social service data to fully characterize and improve the health of New Yorkers. The Bureau of Epidemiology Services (BES) collects, analyzes and communicates data to monitor and improve the health of New Yorkers. BES provides statistical and analytic support for public health surveillance, epidemiologic research, and program evaluations at DOHMH. BES plays a pivotal role for initiating and performing inter and intra agency collaboration projects, including acquiring data, developing study designs and methodologies, analyzing data, and disseminating findings. jobs.title: Senior Drug Checking Epidemiologist, Bureau of Alcohol and Drug Use
jobs.description: The Bureau of Alcohol and Drug Use (BADU) works to close gaps and reduce overall morbidity and mortality related to alcohol and substance use among New Yorkers. BADU develops, implements, and evaluates interventions and prevention strategies through contracting of treatment, recovery and support services; policy analysis and development; epidemiology and surveillance; dissemination of treatment and management guidelines; harm reduction initiatives; public and provider outreach and education; and community involvement and interagency collaboration. The Bureau amplifies the voices of those most impacted and focuses on inequitable structural, social, service, and communication factors that drive disparities. The Office of Research, Surveillance, Policy and Communications within the Bureau of Alcohol and Drug Use is responsible for conducting timely surveillance of alcohol and drug-related morbidity and mortality in NYC, reporting on key trends and disparate impacts by demographic group and neighborhood, conducting drug-checking services and surveillance of the unregulated drug supply in NYC, performing program evaluation and monitoring, and leading community engagement and communications campaigns to educate New Yorkers about alcohol and drug-related health risks.  DUTIES WILL INCLUDE BUT NOT BE LIMITED TO: 1. Serve as data steward for all drug checking data. 2. Extract, clean, manipulate, organize, and analyze data for the bureau’s Drug Checking Program using primarily R, REDCap, Excel and other platforms as needed. 3. Design, conduct, and develop new methods of analyses that will inform future directions of the Drug Checking Program. 4. Create and update data management documentation relating to the Drug Checking Program, including data dictionaries and codebooks, protocols, and methods. 5. Lead preparation and dissemination of data tables, reports, briefs, presentations, and scientific manuscripts to clearly communicate findings and recommendations to a variety of audiences including the public, agency and bureau leadership, other government agencies, and healthcare providers. 6. Lead the development of data visualization and public dissemination of drug checking results collected across New York City sites. 7. Prepare and manage IRB applications for the Drug Checking Program. 8. Represent bureau in collaborations with internal and external partners, and collaborate to align data collection and reporting with bureau monitoring and policy needs. 9. Supervise and mentor the work of a Drug Checking Data Analyst. 10. Perform all other responsibilities and projects as assigned by supervisors.  PREFERRED SKILLS: At least 3-5 years of experience analyzing drug epidemiology-related data in an applied setting using R or similar application • Experience with database management using R, SQL, Microsoft Access, or similar platforms • Survey development experience using REDCap or similar survey building tools • Experience building and maintaining data dashboards or other public-facing online-based dissemination platforms; experience with Datawrapper and Power BI a plus • Experience or familiarity with Git or Github, for team collaboration and code review, a plus • Demonstrated analytical and problem-solving skills • Experience reviewing and editing documents and/or data requests on a tight deadline • Excellent computer skills, including MS Office • Experience with data visualization and reporting of results for various audiences, including community members who use drugs, staff members at harm reduction organizations, and providers • Excellent organizational skills and attention to detail • Passionate about conducting analyses with the end goal of reducing drug-related morbidity and mortality in New York City  Why you should work for us:  - Loan Forgiveness: As a prospective employee of the City of New York, you may be eligible for federal/state loan forgiveness and repayment assistance programs that lessen your payments or even fully forgive your full balance. jobs.title: Senior Manager of Capacity Building, Office of Deputy Commissioner
jobs.description: The Center for Health Equity & Community Wellness (CHECW) seeks to eliminate racial and other inequities resulting in premature mortality. With an unwavering grounding in history and structural analysis, CHECW works to increase visibility of the harm perpetuated by centuries of racist, socially unjust policy while pushing towards redress for the most impacted NYC communities. CHECW addresses inequity across community and healthcare systems in partnership with community, faith-based, and health care organizations. CHECW's work focuses on social determinants of health, including health care organizations. CHECW's work focuses on social determinants of health, including environmental and commercial determinants, and addresses both upstream and downstream factors to improve health and well-being of New Yorkers. CHECW is comprised of the Bureau of Bronx Neighborhood Health, the Bureau of Brooklyn Neighborhood Health, the Bureau of Queens Neighborhood Health, the Bureau of Chronic Disease Prevention, the Bureau of Equitable Health Systems, the Bureau of Finance and Administrative Services. The division's Deputy Commissioner also serves as the Agency's Chief Equity Officer and oversees Race to Justice, the Agency's internal reform effort to help our staff learn what they can do to better address racial health gaps and improve health outcomes for all New Yorkers. The Health Department launched Race to Justice (RTJ) in 2016 as its agency-wide internal transformation initiative. The primary purpose of the initiative is to build the Health Department's capacity to address structural racism and health inequities by promoting anti racism and embedding racial equity and social justice in our policies, processes, and programs, ensuring that our internal and external practices reflect our values without perpetuating injustices. Spearheaded by the RTJMT, the initiative aims to transform the Health Department by building capacity and embedding racial equity and social justice within every aspect of DOHMH to ultimately improve equitable health outcomes for all New Yorkers by: 1) Increasing staff's awareness of how racism and other intersecting systems of oppression operate within institutions, with the knowledge and understanding that NYC institutions, with the knowledge and understanding that NYC institutions, including the Health Department, are not separate and immune from these systemic injustices. 2) Developing staff's skills to address how internal systems of oppression create health equities. 3) Examining how structural racism and other intersecting systems of oppression impact the Health Department's work, decisions, interactions, and priorities. 4) Implementing policies and practices to mitigate the impacts of systems of oppression.   The Office of the Chief Equity Officer seeks to hire a Senior Manager of Capacity Building to join the management team to build internal capacity among staff to advance racial and social justice and the Health Department's equity goals.  DUTIES WILL INCLUDE BUT NOT BE LIMITED TO: • Lead the development and facilitation of communities of practice for agency staff, including equity-focused staff and senior level leadership.  • Organize and/or deliver capacity building trainings and workshops, among other learning activities, focused on embedding equity into daily practices and job responsibilities.  • Evaluate capacity building programs for quality assurance through surveys and analysis of findings.  • Stay abreast of current research, evidence-based best practices, and tools/resources for applying equity in public health.  • Manage, update, and serve as the technical point person for a tool library that includes equity focused tools and resources to assist staff in embedding racial justice and equity.  • Serve as central point of contact for agency equity stakeholder community, including implementing a system of accountability for staff working on projects that advance the goals of the Office of the Chief Equity Officer.  • Connect and coordinate with other team members as it relates to capacity building.  • Contribute to the overall design, strategy, and implementation of Race to Justice activities, as a member of the management team.  PREFERRED SKILLS: Three years of full-time experience in program management, community-based programming, public health, government, or a related field. Excellent oral, written, organizational, and interpersonal communication skills. Ability to manage multiple projects and priorities, work collaboratively across disciplines, and build effective relationships with diverse stakeholders. Strong project management and coordination skills, including the ability to work effectively with government agencies, community organizations, consultants, academic partners, and other external stakeholders  Why you should work for us:  - Loan Forgiveness: As a prospective employee of the City of New York, you may be eligible for federal/state loan forgiveness and repayment assistance programs that lessen your payments or even fully forgive your full balance. jobs.description: The New York City (NYC) Department of Health and Mental Hygiene (DOHMH) is a public health leader serving over 8.4 million New York City residents from diverse ethnic, cultural, and economic backgrounds. The NYC Public Health Laboratory (PHL) is one of the largest local public health laboratories in the United States offering a dynamic and innovative work environment where employees contribute to the health and safety of NYC residents by providing clinical and environmental laboratory testing services. With more than 100 years of leadership in public health, a team of over 200 scientific and support staff are committed to its mission to safeguard the health of all NYC residents by providing quality laboratory testing services that support the priorities of the NYC DOHMH and its community partners to prevent and respond to clinical and environmental public health concerns.   The DOHMH PHL seeks a qualified candidate to serve as a supervisor in the Environmental Sciences Section. This position will play an integral role in laboratory testing and responding to public health threats, including but not limited to COVID-19, vaccine preventable diseases, HIV, Legionella as well as respiratory, foodborne, and waterborne disease outbreaks. This is an excellent opportunity to join our multidisciplinary team, and collaborate with local, state, federal, and academic partners. The supervisor will primarily work within the Water Microbiology Unit at PHL. The units utilize microbiological and molecular microbiological tools to detect and monitor pathogens in drinking and recreational water, and non-potable water systems such as cooling towers. This includes NYC’s beach monitoring and Legionella response programs. ·   DUTIES WILL INCLUDE BUT NOT BE LIMITED TO: • Supervising, training, assigning work, and evaluating the performance of staff. Able to shift priorities in response to rapidly evolving work environment. • Conducting investigations regarding agents related to public health outbreaks using independent judgement and initiative, and performing data analysis on test results. Assisting in the coordination of agency, local and federal partners in investigations. • Performing research to identify and implement new technologies. • Communicating effectively with lab technologists and internal and external partners. • Evaluating data, preparing reports, maintaining records, and assisting in the coordination of research efforts of the Agency. • Maintaining and participating in a program of quality control and assurance; and advising staff on appropriate methods and techniques. • Implementing and monitoring laboratory quality, and health and safety policies and procedures. • Performing or overseeing the design and maintenance of charts, logs, and other records. • Assist with inventory, budgeting, and procurement to ensure that laboratory is properly stocked with reagents and supplies necessary for testing; and ensure that items are properly tracked using inventory management system. • Writes original manuscripts for publication based on data analyses.  PREFERRED SKILLS: • Previous supervisory experience with handling multiple projects and managing people. • Experience working with pathogenic organisms in a BSL2 environment. • Basic microbiology and molecular biology techniques including PCR. • Ability to interpret complex laboratory data and communicate that data to internal and external partners using independent judgement and initiative. • Experience in an environmental or clinical diagnostic testing laboratory. • Ability to generate concise reports regarding data generated during testing, verifications, etc.  Why you should work for us:  - Loan Forgiveness: As a prospective employee of the City of New York, you may be eligible for federal/state loan forgiveness and repayment assistance programs that lessen your payments or even fully forgive your full balance.
