jobs.title: Team Lead: TST for SU & EAU, Bureau of Tuberculosis Control
jobs.description: The Team Lead for TST (SU & EAU) directs tuberculosis surveillance, environmental infection control, and outbreak prevention strategies across DOH chest centers, shelters, and high-risk facilities. In this role, you will manage a multidisciplinary team of research scientists, epidemiologists, and public health advisors conducting quantitative research on airborne tuberculosis detection, managing employee tuberculin skin testing (TST) programs, and overseeing patient isolation protocols. You will evaluate airborne mitigation technologies—such as UVGI, negative pressure, and ACH air-flow systems—to recommend compliant products and establish evidence-based safety guidelines. Additionally, you will oversee outbreak investigations, represent the TB Control Program across internal and external committees, and author scientific papers to publish findings and advance environmental infection control practices statewide.  DUTIES WILL INCLUDE BUT NOT BE LIMITED TO: - Direct activities and staff of the Tuberculin Skin Testing (TST) Surveillance Unit to meet requirements and fulfill scientific objectives. Ensures that staff in the TST Unit conduct periodic and serial testing of targeted high-risk DOH employees. - Direct activities and staff of the Environmental Affairs Unit to meet requirements and fulfill scientific objectives. - Directs respiratory protection fit testing by the TST Unit and the Environmental Affairs Unit for designated staff in BTBC. - Performs employee evaluations - Serve as a resource to the BTBC for environmental issues pertaining to TB infection control devices and measures including UVG lamps, negatives air pressure, ventilation, and respiratory prevention. - Consults on referrals for patients on home isolation - Provides specialty guidance to Bureau and DOH staff associated with TB outbreaks. - Directs TB related infection control surveys, evaluation, and assessments. - Provides recommendations on infection control and the implementation of environmental controls understanding the standards and guidelines set by the Joint Commission of Accreditation of Health Organizations (JCAHO), CDC, OSHA, PESH, and NIOSH. - Writes technical reports, recommendations, and protocols related to TB transmission. - Plans and implements protocols to develop effective coordination of efforts of the Program and outside projects. - Consults and represents the Program with internal and external entities regarding environmental control of tuberculosis and/or related projects, including providing information regarding design, methodology, sampling procedures, skin testing procedures, and technical matters - Conducts research as indicated, writes papers, and publishes on environmental control of TB  Preferred skills: - Excellent written and oral communication skills  - Experience in research design and intervention - jobs.title: Technical Assistance Specialist, Bureau of Alcohol and Drug Use
jobs.description: The Bureau of Alcohol and Drug Use (BADU) works to close gaps and reduce overall morbidity and mortality related to alcohol and substance use among New Yorkers. BADU develops, implements, and evaluates interventions and prevention strategies through contracting of treatment, recovery and support services; policy analysis and development; epidemiology and surveillance; dissemination of treatment and management guidelines; harm reduction initiatives; public and provider outreach and education; and community involvement and interagency collaboration. The Bureau amplifies the voices of those most impacted and focuses on inequitable structural, social, service, and communication factors that drive disparities.  The Overdose Education and Naloxone Distribution Unit (OENDU) within BADU develops and implements initiatives to reduce and prevent opioid overdose deaths in New York City. The Unit provides naloxone, training, and technical assistance to approximately 350 Opioid Overdose Prevention Programs (OOPPs) across New York City. OOPPs provide community-based overdose prevention, recognition, and response education and distribute naloxone directly to community members.  The Technical Assistance Specialist will provide technical assistance and programmatic guidance to current and potential opioid overdose prevention programs (OOPPs) on implementing successful overdose prevention and naloxone distribution programming, with the goal of preventing overdose deaths in New York City. Prevention Training Team to plan, schedule, and deliver Training of Dispensers for OOPPs and/or Training of Responders for community members as needed •	Contribute to the development of new materials and resources aimed at preventing overdose and improving OOPP efficiency •	Assemble naloxone kits to be dispensed in trainings and maintain records for all kits dispensed •	Provide support for packing jobs.title: Vector-borne Disease Epidemiologist, Bureau of Communicable Diseases
jobs.description: The Division of Disease Control’s mission is to safeguard the health of New Yorkers through identification, surveillance, treatment, control, and prevention of infectious diseases, which is achieved through varied and interrelated endeavors of its seven Bureaus. The Bureau of Communicable Disease (BCD), part of the Division of Disease Control, is responsible for the surveillance, prevention, and control of over 70 infectious diseases including foodborne, enteric, waterborne, respiratory (including COVID-19), zoonotic, and vector-borne diseases.  Position Summary:  This position is in the Zoonotic and Vector-Borne Disease Unit (ZVDU) within the Bureau of Communicable Disease (BCD). ZVDU is responsible for overseeing the surveillance for reportable, new, high profile, and emerging vector-borne diseases that are reportable in New York City. Vectorborne diseases include, but are not limited to Lyme disease, babesiosis, anaplasmosis, alpha-gal syndrome and certain high-profile diseases such as legionellosis and cyclosporiasis.   ZVDU is recruiting an experienced epidemiologist and data analyst to work under the Research Scientist to perform and enhance Lyme disease surveillance as well as contribute to similar efforts for other vectorborne diseases. The person will have experience in epidemiology, data management, and analysis, outreach and education for the public and human and animal health providers, as well as participate in a wide range of activities, with an emphasis on vectorborne diseases, and direct oversight of Lyme disease surveillance. They will be a collaborative partner working closely with the Division of Environmental Health, the Public Health Laboratory, and local, state, and federal partners.  Job Duties and Responsibilities:  •	Assist the Research Scientist II in the development and enhancement of surveillance practices, updating (and developing when needed) disease case investigation protocols and standardized investigation case forms used for tick-borne diseases,  •	Conduct case investigations and other activities required for routine surveillance of Lyme disease, •	Participate in the collection, management and analysis of quality data for research and surveillance purposes,  •	Conduct quality assurance of data, •	Maintain, summarize and report on tick-borne disease data from the BCD surveillance system •	Conduct literature reviews of recent and relevant research as it relates to our understanding our diseases of interest, •	Work collaboratively with colleagues in Environmental Health and other agencies and organizations, •	Participate in ZVDU fieldwork which may include tick dragging as well as other fieldwork opportunities, •	Participate in large BCD outbreak investigations as needed, •	Supervise seasonal college interns, •	Conduct outreach to the medical and veterinary communities,  •	Participate in agency-wide response activations as needed  Preferred Skills:   •	Experience with disease surveillance, infectious diseases, and database management •	Ability to work independently and in teams to collect and analyze data, including leading outbreak and cluster investigations •	Excellent written and verbal communication skills with the ability to interpret data and convey concepts clearly and concisely  •	Proficiency with SAS (programming and analysis) or other analytic software, Adobe Acrobat, and MS Office software; ability to learn new data systems quickly, document in the data systems, and comply with data integrity and security to safeguard all personal identifiable information •	Flexibility and adaptability are key attributes for this position; The Bureau amplifies the voices of those most impacted and focuses on inequitable structural, social, service, and communication factors that drive disparities.  DUTIES WILL INCLUDE BUT NOT BE LIMITED TO: Provide research and data support for the expansion of Relay at new hospitals in collaboration with hospital leadership. Conduct research to develop protocols, communications materials, and presentations. Provide regular supervision to full-time and part-time Wellness Advocates in their role supporting patients following a non-fatal overdose and conducting research. Review reports from the program’s database and dashboard on a regular basis to support data-driven supervision. Utilize the program's database to monitor Wellness Advocates' cases to ensure quality assurance standards are being met for research, data collection and data entry, decision making, and overall documentation. Collaborate with colleagues to support the program’s reporting requirements and record observations, including by performing internal auditing activities and assessing participant records. jobs.description: The Division of Disease Control’s mission is to safeguard the health of New Yorkers through identification, surveillance, treatment, control, and prevention of infectious diseases, which is achieved through varied and interrelated endeavors of its seven Bureaus. The Bureau of Communicable Disease (BCD), part of the Division of Disease Control, is responsible for the surveillance, prevention, and control of over 70 infectious diseases including foodborne, enteric, waterborne, respiratory (including COVID-19), zoonotic, and vector-borne diseases. This position is in the Zoonotic and Vector-Borne Disease Unit (ZVDU) within the Bureau of Communicable Disease (BCD). ZVDU is responsible for overseeing the surveillance for new, high profile, and emerging zoonotic and vector-borne diseases in people and animals that are reportable in New York City. Human diseases include, but are not limited to, leptospirosis, dengue, chikungunya, Lyme disease, and babesiosis, and certain high-profile diseases such as legionellosis, West Nile virus, cyclosporiasis, rabies and avian influenza. Animal diseases reportable to ZVDU include H5N1 and other avian influenza virus, brucellosis, rabies, New World screwworm, and leptospirosis.   ZVDU is recruiting an experienced epidemiologist and data analyst. jobs.description: The New York County District Attorney’s Office has an immediate opening for an Investigative Analyst in its Crime Strategies Unit (CSU). The Crime Strategies Unit proactively gathers and analyzes crime data and intelligence to drive the Office’s strategies on crime reduction and public safety. Members of CSU work closely with the New York City Police Department to identify and study crime trends, as well as groups and individuals most responsible for driving crimes that impact our communities, including violent crime, theft, and fraud. CSU also supports the mission of the Gun Violence Strategic Partnership, which brings together both state and federal law enforcement agencies to combat gun violence throughout New York City. Investigative analysts are responsible for providing CSU with investigative, analytical, and data manipulation support. The position requires a critical thinker with a strong combination of data skills and technological savvy. Candidates should also possess strong organizational and communication skills, as CSU relies on analysts’ work product in presentations to the highest levels of the District Attorney’s Office as well as law enforcement and community partners.    Responsibilities include, but are not limited to:  •	Gather, analyze, and process data using industry-current and in-house proprietary applications to produce a complete model of crime trends in Manhattan neighborhoods. •	Assist in developing and implementing intelligence-driven prosecution strategies targeting priority offenders. •	Analyze intelligence to identify gun violence drivers in conjunction with local, state, and federal partners. •	Gather, organize, and analyze firearm traces and ballistic comparison reports and data. •	Support day-to-day unit functions as needed. •	Create descriptive presentations and reports using statistical analysis, including cleaning and synthesizing data, and reconciling qualitative and quantitative data sources. •	Perform a full range of administrative and paralegal duties as needed.   In addition to the Minimum Qualification Requirements, all candidates must possess the following:  •	Level 1 – Bachelor’s degree from an accredited college and one (1) year of experience either as a paralegal in the criminal justice field or equivalent.          •	Level 2 -  Bachelor’s degree from an accredited college and two (2) years of experience either as a paralegal in the criminal justice field or equivalent.        •	Level 3 -  Bachelor’s degree from an accredited college and three (3) years of experience either as a paralegal in the criminal justice field or equivalent.   *Master’s degree can be substituted for years of experience. *   Preferred Requirements/Skills:  •	Proficiency with Microsoft Office products. Excel experience (pivot tables; charts; functions; etc.) preferred. •	Familiarity with data mapping, including geocoding preferred; and a fast learner regarding new technology tools and software. Experience using Photoshop; ArcGIS; i2 Analyst Notebook; etc. a plus. •	Superior organizational, time management, writing, and communication skills are essential. •	Capable of building institutional relationships with community residents and organizations, police, and other law enforcement agencies. •	Ability to effectively communicate investigative results to other team members, and to testify in court if necessary. •	Experience in the Criminal Justice System preferred. •	An understanding of general practices related to legal records management, data protection, and privacy/confidentiality. jobs.title: Data Quality Analyst
jobs.description: The Fire Department of the City of New York (FDNY) is the largest Fire Department in the United States and universally is recognized as the world's busiest and most highly skilled emergency response agency. The Department's main goal is to provide fire protection, emergency medical care, and other critical public safety services to residents and visitors in the five boroughs. FDNY members are sworn to serve and protect life and property and the Department works to continually educate the public in fire, life safety and disaster preparedness, along with enforcing public safety codes. Since its inception in 1865, FDNY has helped lead efforts to make New York the safest big city in the nation. This accomplishment requires a steadfast and daily commitment to maintaining the Department's core values.  The FDNY Bureau of Enterprise Technology manages key departmental initiatives and drives data-driven decision-making. Its Data Quality unit is responsible for generating actionable insights through analysis, reporting, and visualizations. This unit also ensures accountability and transparency by compiling metrics for the Mayor's Management Report (MMR) and producing datasets for NYC Open Data.  The Fire Department of the City of New York (FDNY) seeks a full-time City Research Scientist, L2 in the Data Quality Unit. With latitude for independent initiative and judgement, the Data Quality Analyst will assist the Department’s in the making evidence-based decisions. Day-to-day responsibilities focus on data quality and insight delivery. This includes rigorously performing data quality checks and anomaly detection. The Data Quality Analyst will also support the building of interactive dashboards, primarily using Tableau and modern Python frameworks (Dash/Streamlit). Other core duties include swift fulfilling of ad-hoc data requests and designing appropriate metrics to track and report on departmental performance. This position will also participate in community outreach, especially in the context of Open Data which could include responding to public inquiries, representing the Department at Open Data Events and gathering feedback from the community. This is a crucial function that connects the FDNY's internal data efforts with the public, leveraging data transparency to enhance safety and build trust. Minimum qualifications: 1.  For Assignment Level I (only physical, biological and environmental sciences and public health) A master's degree from an accredited college or university with a specialization in an appropriate field of physical, biological or environmental science or in public health.  To be appointed to Assignment Level II and above, candidates must have:  1. A doctorate degree from an accredited college or university with specialization in an appropriate field of physical, biological, environmental or social science and one year of full-time experience in a responsible supervisory, administrative or research capacity in the appropriate field of specialization; or  2. A master's degree from an accredited college or university with specialization in an appropriate field of physical, biological, environmental or social science and three years of responsible full-time research experience in the appropriate field of specialization; or  3. Education and/or experience which is equivalent to "1" or "2" above. However, all candidates must have at least a master's degree in an appropriate field of specialization and at least two years of experience described in "2" above. Two years as a City Research Scientist Level I can be substituted for the experience required in "1" and "2" above.    NOTE:  Probationary Period  Appointments to this position are subject to a minimum probationary period of one year. Preferred skills: Excellent communication and presentation skills, skilled in creating data visualizations and metrics. Excellent programming skills in SQL and Python. Knowledge of basic statistics.

jobs.description: Who We Are Great Minds is a high-growth, mission-driven organization founded by educators in 2007. As a for-profit, Public Benefit Corporation, we believe all students deserve access to meaningful, challenging content—and all teachers deserve tools that are intuitive, effective, and built for the realities of today’s classrooms. We develop high-quality, knowledge-rich math, science and ELA curricula grounded in research and designed in collaboration with educators. Our materials reflect real classroom needs and are built to drive lasting student outcomes. We are committed to usability, coherence, and practical implementation—supporting teachers not just through curriculum, but with professional learning, purposeful technology, and responsive service that enable strong adoption and impact. What We Build Our products— Eureka Math and Eureka Math², Wit & Wisdom , Geodes , and the newly launched Arts & Letters ELA —are trusted by thousands of schools and districts nationwide. Eureka Math is the most widely used math curriculum in the U.S., and is focused on balancing conceptual understanding, procedural fluency, and application. Wit & Wisdom® and Arts & Letters ELA™ anchor our reading strategy with content-rich, grade-level instruction that integrates literature, history, and the arts, grounded in the science of reading. Geodes® complements our reading suite with decodable texts that pair phonics with meaningful content to support early literacy. These programs reflect a shared belief in high expectations, joyful rigor, and deep respect for educators and students. Where We’re Headed Great Minds is entering a new stage of growth and product maturity. We are focused on building more connected, customer-informed experiences across the full educator journey—from curriculum to professional learning to platform and support. Our long-term vision is to become a true partner in impact—not just delivering curriculum, but supporting educators in achieving outcomes at scale. Job Purpose Reporting to the Director of Policy, the Lead Policy Analyst will act as a senior-level individual contributor, operating as the team’s primary subject matter expert and analytical engine. This role will take ownership of Great Minds’ policy intelligence work by tracking and interpreting the federal, state, and local landscape to ensure the organization is well-positioned to engage and influence. The position will bring depth, initiative, and independent judgment to complex policy questions and will translate findings into strategies that meaningfully shape how Great Minds engages with policymakers, state agencies, and K–12 stakeholders. Responsibilities Serve as the team’s primary analytical resource for K–12 policy trends—independently framing issues, synthesizing intelligence across federal, state, and local levels, and contributing substantively to Great Minds’ company-wide point of view on factors shaping the adoption and implementation of high-quality instructional materials. Own the tracking and monitoring of state and local legislation and policy; identify and escalate emerging policy trends with clear analytical context and recommended implications for the organization. Lead projects that examine how legislative mandates shape policy action at the local, regional, and state levels; develop findings that are rigorous, accessible, and directly connected to Great Minds’ strategic priorities. Translate regional trend analysis into concrete recommendations that help shape the organization’s policy engagement strategy; identifying where and how Great Minds should invest, focus and build relationships. Ensure internal stakeholders are equipped to understand and act on the policy environment by producing clear briefings, frameworks, and recommendations tailored to diverse audiences across the organization. Represent Great Minds externally at policy conferences and sector events, strengthening the organization’s credibility and visibility among policymakers and K–12 influencers. Requirements 7+ years of experience in K–12 policy, applied research, or a closely related discipline, with a track record of owning and advancing substantive policy work Proven ability to independently drive research projects from problem framing through strategic recommendation, with strong judgment about when to escalate and how to prioritize Sophisticated command of quantitative and qualitative research methodologies, with the ability to synthesize complex findings into accessible, compelling narratives for varied audiences Proven ability to manage competing priorities and stakeholder demands, balancing ongoing policy monitoring with discrete research projects and time-sensitive requests from across the organization Deep familiarity with state and local policy development processes, including legislative tracking and stakeholder engagement Demonstrated experience converting a complex policy landscape into clear strategic priorities and actionable plans Required Education Bachelor’s degree Preferred Advanced degree in public policy, education policy, or a related field Status Full-time Location Remote The expected base salary range for this position is $107,000-$120,000, however the offered salary may be higher or lower than the above range dependent on numerous factors including, but not limited to location, work experience, skills and internal equity considerations. The base salary is not inclusive of benefits or other incentives. A cover letter and resume are required to be considered for this position. New employees will be required to successfully complete a background check. If in the course of the application or hiring process with Great Minds you are contacted through another domain, are requested to provide banking or other sensitive information, or you note any other suspicious activity, please contact security@greatminds.org Great Minds is an equal opportunity employer. jobs.description: By working at Harvard University, you join a vibrant community that advances Harvard's world-changing mission in meaningful ways, inspires innovation and collaboration, and builds skills and expertise. We are dedicated to creating a diverse and welcoming environment where everyone can thrive. Why join Harvard Medical School? Harvard Medical School's mission is to nurture a diverse, inclusive community dedicated to alleviating suffering and improving health and well-being for all through excellence in teaching and learning, discovery and scholarship, and service and leadership. You’ll be at the heart of biomedical discovery, education, and innovation, working alongside world-renowned faculty and a community dedicated to improving human health. This is more than a job - it’s an opportunity to shape the future of medicine. Harvard Medical School Information Systems seeks a Business Systems Analyst professional skilled in leading requirements elicitation, journey mapping, business process redesign, and user-centered design. This position will support the Harvard Integrated Life Sciences (HILS) Administration and will design, develop, and implement solutions to streamline HILS operations and data collection processes. The position will collaborate regularly with the HILS Director of Academic Administration and Education Staff to translate business needs into technology strategies and systems requirements. The position will participate in the full software development lifecycle (SDLC) from project inception through ongoing production support, including data analysis, testing, and training. The position will require experience with desktop, mobile, or web-based software applications and relational databases with a service delivery approach. Familiarity with Peoplesoft Campus Solutions and/or Oracle Business Intelligence Enterprise Suite and/or Oracle Analytics will be a plus. The ideal candidate will be energized by solving problems in new and innovative ways. You are comfortable working in an ever-changing environment and have the ability to engage with stakeholders to identify minimal viable product for frequent delivery of new technology solutions. Core Duties: Research, design, documentation, implementation, configuration, and validation of solutions to business needs. Collaborate with stakeholders to translate business needs into technology strategies, systems requirements and scoping of IT projects. Lead definition of system requirements, gap analysis, user journey mapping and identification of feasible alternative solutions that meet defined business objectives. Document and refine current state and future state system processes, design and review prototypes to meet key gaps and processes and build support from technology stakeholders in solutions. Define Agile user stories that meet business requirements and application features, data conversion, systems integration, security, or customizations. Identify user story prioritization and sprint content collaboratively with the stakeholders and IT team to ensure effective delivery of IT projects. Assess business implications of technology applications and the impact on current and future business environment. Identify process, practice, or policy change recommendations based on input from stakeholders, comprehension of the subject area, and awareness of current or new system’s potential capabilities. Assist with change management to ensure that systems are understood and adopted by users. Develop training materials and work with change agents and trainers on training approach and delivery. Partners with HUIT, School officials, and internal IT to assess system integration opportunities. Basic Qualifications: Minimum of two years’ post-secondary education or relevant work experience. Additional Qualifications and Skills: Bachelor's degree preferred. 5+ years' experience in defining requirements for desktop, mobile, or web-based software applications and relational databases preferred. Familiarity with desktop, mobile, or web-based software applications and relational databases with a service delivery approach. Familiarity with Peoplesoft Campus Solutions and/or Oracle Business Intelligence Enterprise Suite and/or Oracle Analytics will be a plus. Demonstrated team performance delivering technology solutions with a service mindset approach. Familiarity with the agile methodology and experienced working with agile frameworks and tools. Strong analytical and critical thinking skills to solve complex issues. Strong ability to communicate both verbally and in writing with internal and external teams. Ability to prioritize and multitask, deadline and detail oriented. Troubleshooting skills, problem resolution, project management and technology evaluation to meet business requirements. Certificates and Licenses: Completion of Harvard IT Academy specified foundational courses (or external equivalent) preferred. Standard Hours/Schedule: 35 hours per week. Work is primarily carried out remotely with monthly in-office anchor days for local employees. Visa Sponsorship Information: Harvard University is unable to provide visa sponsorship for this position. jobs.description: By working at Harvard University, you join a vibrant community that advances Harvard's world-changing mission in meaningful ways, inspires innovation and collaboration, and builds skills and expertise. We are dedicated to creating a diverse and welcoming environment where everyone can thrive. Why join the Harvard Graduate School of Education? The Harvard Graduate School of Education (HGSE) is a diverse community of learners, teachers, and employees who are passionate about changing the world through education and striving for maximum impact in the field of education. Many choose to work at the Harvard Graduate School of Education because they believe in our mission and are excited by our vision for the future. We have a reputation as a great place to work, for our excellent leadership, and we are a strong community that values diversity. For more information about HGSE, its programs, research, and faculty, please visit: www.gse.harvard.edu . Job Summary: At the Center for Education Policy Research at Harvard University (CEPR) our mission is to transform education through the power of quality evidence. We believe that if we want to dramatically improve educational outcomes for all children, evidence must play a critical role. The Math Teaching and Teacher Learning team at CEPR provides math-specific professional development to teachers and coaches to help improve math instruction. Our current grant-funded projects seek to develop and test an expanded math-specific coach training program (M-Powering Teacher Coaching) that uses machine-learning automated feedback and AI-enhanced coaching tools. The Data Scientist will contribute to this and other projects that connect rigorous educational research with practical tools for teachers, instructional coaches, and education leaders. This person will oversee, manage, and lead analysis and application of complex datasets, and contribute to the integration of research insights into innovative educational tools and cutting-edge products. They will be joining a team with faculty lead and Principal Investigator, Heather Hill, and collaborators at higher education research institutions, professional learning organizations, curriculum providers, and Enterprise AI firm(s). Job-Specific Responsibilities: Key responsibilities of the Data Scientist include: Data and Research Infrastructure: Organizes, cleans, and prepares structured and unstructured data (e.g., video, audio, text) for AI modeling and analysis. Develops and documents codebooks, annotation protocols, data dictionaries, and other research procedures. Builds and documents reproducible workflows for data processing, annotation, statistical analysis, and modeling. Supports shared practices for version control, code review, data security, and reproducible research. Maintains organized project files, code repositories, data documentation, and analytic records. Analysis and Measurement Development Conduct data science work across grant-funded projects focused on teaching, instructional coaching, curriculum, and artificial intelligence in education. Applies statistical, machine learning, natural language processing, and generative AI methods as appropriate. Coordinates and executes the development and evaluation of automated measures related to teaching, coaching, curriculum implementation, and teacher learning. Supports pilot studies and evaluation activities related to usability, implementation, coaching, and teacher experience. Product Development and Dissemination Helps integrate research measures and findings into education tools and user interfaces. Contributes to research papers, reports, public goods, funder deliverables, and other project materials (e.g., tables, figures, visualization, presentations, and technical documentation) Project Management and Cross-team Collaboration Manages timelines and deliverables across one or more grant-funded workstreams Collaborates with researchers, educators, software developers, and external partners such as Enterprise AI firm(s) to support project goals. Oversees internal working groups to deliver on tasks and milestones Performs other duties as assigned. Basic Qualifications Bachelor’s degree in Data Science, Statistics, Computer Science, Economics, Mathematics, Education, Social Science, or a related field. Relevant experience, which may include professional, research, internship, or concurrent-with-baccalaureate experience in data science, statistical programming, machine learning, educational research, or a related field. Must have strong organizational, communication, and problem-solving skills, with the ability to work independently and collaboratively. Occasional travel may be required to support project meetings, trainings, pilot activities, or other research-related events. Candidates should submit a resume or curriculum vitae and cover letter describing their relevant experience and interest in the position. All candidates invited to the in-person/hybrid interview may be asked to complete a task and/or submit a sample program. This is a full-time, one-year term appointment beginning on the date of hire, with the possibility of continuation based on funding, performance, and departmental needs. The work arrangement is remote, subject to project and departmental needs. Additional Qualifications and Skills: Master’s degree in data science, statistics, computer science, education, economics, social science, or a related field preferred. Experience with R, Python, Stata, or a similar programming language preferred. Experience with machine learning, natural language processing, generative AI, or automated scoring strongly preferred. Experience with data annotation, codebook development, or qualitative and quantitative coding preferred. Familiarity with building reproducible workflows for data cleaning, processing, analysis, or modeling preferred. Familiarity with version control, databases, APIs, or collaborative software development preferred. Experience with K-12 education data or education research is a plus. Experience with mathematics teaching and learning is a plus. Interest in improving education through responsible and evidence-based uses of artificial intelligence; commitment to equity, diversity, inclusion, and belonging. Appointment End Date: One year from date of hire Standard Hours/Schedule: 35 hours per week Compensation Range/Rate (including Shift Differential if applicable): $90,000 - $95,000 commensurate with experience Visa Sponsorship Information: Harvard University is unable to provide visa sponsorship for this position Pre-Employment Screening: Identity and Education Work Format Details This position has been determined by school or unit leaders that the duties and responsibilities can effectively be performed fully remotely at a non-Harvard location. Employees in fully remote positions must work all scheduled hours in a Harvard registered state in compliance with the University’s Policy on Employment Outside of Massachusetts . At the discretion of the department, fully remote employees may occasionally be required on site at a Harvard location. Certain visa types and funding sources may limit work location. Individuals must meet work location sponsorship requirements prior to employment. Salary Grade and Ranges This position is salary grade level 057. Please visit Harvard's Salary Ranges to view the corresponding salary range and related information. Benefits Harvard offers a comprehensive benefits package that is designed to support a healthy work-life balance and your physical, mental and financial wellbeing. Because here, you are what matters. Our benefits include, but are not limited to: Generous paid time off including parental leave Medical, dental, and vision health insurance coverage starting on day one Retirement plans with university contributions Wellbeing and mental health resources Support for families and caregivers Professional development opportunities including tuition assistance and reimbursement Commuter benefits, discounts and campus perks Learn more about these and additional benefits on our Benefits & Wellbeing Page . EEO/Non-Discrimination Commitment Statement Harvard University is committed to equal opportunity and non-discrimination . We seek talent from all parts of society and the world, and we strive to ensure everyone at Harvard thrives. Our differences help our community advance Harvard's academic purposes. Harvard has an equal employment opportunity policy that outlines our commitment to prohibiting discrimination on the basis of race, ethnicity, color, national origin, sex, sexual orientation, gender identity, veteran status, religion, disability, or any other characteristic protected by law or identified in the university's non-discrimination policy . Harvard's equal employment opportunity policy and non-discrimination policy help all community members participate fully in work and campus life free from harassment and discrimination.

jobs.title: Analytics & Reporting Engineer for the Division of Strategic Operations & Analytics
jobs.description: About the Agency:  The Department of Housing Preservation and Development (HPD) oversees housing standards across all 3.7 million homes in New York City. As the nation’s largest municipal housing agency, HPD is responsible for building and preserving affordable housing, protecting tenants from harassment and displacement, and holding landlords accountable across the five boroughs. Under Commissioner Dina Levy and the Mamdani Administration, HPD is pursuing an ambitious housing agenda focused on the needs of New York’s tenants. With a broad set of tools including standards enforcement, tenant resources, and the creation of new affordable housing, HPD is committed to making New York City a more affordable place for renters and homeowners alike.  Your Team:  The Office of Policy and Strategy (OPS) leverage its expertise to guide and support HPD and its many Offices in their efforts to deepen their impact, optimize their efficiency, and become more data-driven, climate-adaptive, and mission-focused. As part of OPS, the Division of Strategic Operations and Analytics (SOA) works to increase HPD's impact by analyzing and improving operations agency-wide. SOA does this by clarifying HPD program missions, objectives, and stakeholders; implementing initiatives that advance HPD's goals; analyzing data to deliver actionable insights to HPD programs; and increasing the agency's overall ability to leverage data.  Your Impact:  As the Analytics & Reporting Engineer within SOA, you will play a key role in making HPD’s data more accessible, reliable, and reusable to support reporting and analytics. By building well-structured datasets, automations and data flows, you will help SOA and other HPD offices turn data into key reporting and metrics that support key agency programs for New Yorkers.   Your Role:  Your role will focus on hands-on development of data pipelines, curating datasets and data flows in SQL Server and building reusable scripts and code to support reporting and analytics work for agency programs such as homeless placement services, homebuyer assistance, housing distress & compliance, and fair housing work. You will also create and maintain reports and dashboards, or related dataflows/models. Exercising independent judgement and initiative, you will implement solutions through scalable data models, automated workflows, and well-structured datasets and BI data flows - to enable more efficient reporting, research, and analytics for key agency programs.   Your Responsibilities:  •	Build and maintain core datasets, data models, and dashboards to support key program reporting and analytics •	Build and automate Python-based data cleaning and integration pipelines — merging data across siloed source systems and using automation tools — to support reporting needs for housing placements, fair housing and more. •	Load cleaned datasets into SQL Server and connect to BI tools (e.g. Power BI) to support reporting/dashboarding. •	Implement basic code validation, testing, and documentation practices to keep analytics scripts and datasets reliable and maintainable. •	Document code standards and workflows so datasets and scripts remain usable/maintainable by the team over time. •	Apply data engineering skills and creative collaboration techniques to address technical issues and drive the approach for the team   Preferred skills   •	Inquisitive, self-motivated problem-solver who is passionate about making organizations more data-driven •	Comfortable working in a fast-moving, resource-constrained environment with messy data and legacy systems; motivated by rolling up your sleeves and building practical tools that make a real impact on people's lives. •	Experience building or supporting data pipelines (ETL/ELT) — extracting, cleaning, and transforming data from multiple sources. •	Experience working with relational databases (e.g., SQL Server or similar) •	Some experience with BI data modeling (preferably Power BI or similar) is a plus •	Familiarity with source control and version control workflows (e.g., Azure DevOps Repos) •	Strong interpersonal and organizational skills; able to ask thoughtful questions and collaborate across teams •	Strong aptitude for learning new tools and technologies independently using online resources •	Technical skills: SQL, Python, Power BI data modeling (DAX, Power Query M), and data modeling fundamentals Minimum qualifications: 1.  For Assignment Level I (only physical, biological and environmental sciences and public health) A master's degree from an accredited college or university with a specialization in an appropriate field of physical, biological or environmental science or in public health.  To be appointed to Assignment Level II and above, candidates must have:  1. A doctorate degree from an accredited college or university with specialization in an appropriate field of physical, biological, environmental or social science and one year of full-time experience in a responsible supervisory, administrative or research capacity in the appropriate field of specialization; or  2. A master's degree from an accredited college or university with specialization in an appropriate field of physical, biological, environmental or social science and three years of responsible full-time research experience in the appropriate field of specialization; or  3. Education and/or experience which is equivalent to "1" or "2" above. However, all candidates must have at least a master's degree in an appropriate field of specialization and at least two years of experience described in "2" above. Two years as a City Research Scientist Level I can be substituted for the experience required in "1" and "2" above.    NOTE:  Probationary Period  Appointments to this position are subject to a minimum probationary period of one year. Preferred skills:

As the nation’s largest municipal housing agency, HPD is responsible for building and preserving affordable housing, protecting tenants from harassment and displacement, and holding landlords accountable across the five boroughs. With a broad set of tools including standards enforcement, tenant resources, and the creation of new affordable housing, HPD is committed to making New York City a more affordable place for renters and homeowners alike.    Your Team:  Housing Preservation & Development Technology (HPD Tech) is the IT division within HPD. The Office of HPD Tech leads the agency’s effort to transform HPD through technology by promoting productivity and eliminating manual processing, shrinking costs, and increasing the pace of work. HPD Tech works to improve effectiveness of business processes using core applications for flawless execution. HPD Tech empowers decision makers with access to quality (complete and accurate) information to anticipate and pro-actively react to building, neighborhood and market conditions.   The Office of HPDTech is composed of 9 units: CIO, Budget, Enterprise Architecture, Ideation, Infrastructure Network and Systems, Planning & Compliance, Product Area, Release & Service Management, and Security  Your Impact:  As the Assistant Cloud Administrator for the Division of HPD TECH: The Assistant Cloud Administrator works to maintain the infrastructure and functionality of an Agency’s cloud environments also utilized by Section8\HAS. You will assist the clients in installing and troubleshooting clients to access their cloud services, while working alongside the cloud Administrator to ensure that cloud services continue to function and the service level agreements for function and availability are maintained. You will create, maintain and troubleshoot all parts of the HPD cloud environments with heavy focus on the Section 8 \ HAS Elite on AVD environment within Azure.  Your Role:  Your role will be to assist the HPDTECH Cloud Administrator(s) in all day-to-day duties including but not limited to what is mentioned in the responsibilities and skills required in this document. Minimum qualifications: (1) A baccalaureate degree from an accredited college, including or supplemented by twenty-four (24) semester credits in computer science or a related computer field and two (2) years of satisfactory full-time software experience in designing, programming, debugging, maintaining, implementing, and enhancing computer software applications, systems programming, systems analysis and design, data communication software, or database design and programming, including one year in a project leader capacity or as a major contributor on a complex project; or  (2) A four-year high school diploma or its educational equivalent and six (6) years of full-time satisfactory software experience as described in “1" above, including one year in a project leader capacity or as a major contributor on a complex project; or  (3) A satisfactory combination of education and experience that is equivalent to (1) or (2) above. College education may be substituted for up to two years of the required experience in (2) above on the basis that sixty (60) semester credits from an accredited college is equated to one year of experience. A masters degree in computer science or a related computer field may be substituted for one year of the required experience in (1) or (2) above. However, all candidates must have a four year high school diploma or its educational equivalent, plus at least one (1) year of satisfactory full-time software experience in a project leader capacity or as a major contributor on a complex project.  NOTE: In order to have your experience accepted as Project Leader or Major Contributor experience, you must explain in detail how your experience qualifies you as a project leader or as a major contributor. jobs.description: About the Agency:  The Department of Housing Preservation and Development (HPD) oversees housing standards across all 3.7 million homes in New York City.   As the nation’s largest municipal housing agency, HPD is responsible for building and preserving affordable housing, protecting tenants from harassment and displacement, and holding landlords accountable across the five boroughs. Under Commissioner Dina Levy and the Mamdani Administration, HPD is pursuing an ambitious housing agenda focused on the needs of New York’s tenants. With a broad set of tools including standards enforcement, tenant resources, and the creation of new affordable housing, HPD is committed to making New York City a more affordable place for renters and homeowners alike. [GS1.1]    Your Team The Compliance Specialist for Lead Hazard Control & Healthy Homes will be a key member of the Compliance & Strategy team within the agency’s Office of Compliance & Risk Management (CRM). This Office includes various compliance, oversight, and hearing functions to ensure fairness, consistency, and equity in both our external and internal engagement. CRM collaborates with programs across HPD to ensure the agency and its partners comply with laws (federal, state, and city), regulatory requirements, policies, and procedures. CRM includes the following Divisions and units: •	Compliance & Strategy •	Economic Opportunity & Regulatory Compliance •	Audit Support   •	Adjudications •	Public Information  Your Impact CRM is responsible for overseeing the agency’s compliance and risk management functions, liaising with the units and staff responsible for relevant compliance responsibilities, audit responses, site standard adherence for financed construction work, public-facing appeals and hearings, and managing risk for the agency. The Compliance Specialist for Lead Hazard Control & Healthy Homes will have the opportunity to use their expertise to provide leadership and technical assistance in support of health and safety requirements and compliance best practices throughout the agency, with a focus on environmental hazards. This role will also provide a unique opportunity to help strengthen agency compliance culture and ensure compliance is seamlessly incorporated into HPD program administration and operations.  Your Role Reporting to the Executive Director of Compliance & Strategy, the Compliance Specialist for Lead-Hazard Control & Healthy Homes will manage cross-agency compliance of regulatory requirements and strengthen agency compliance by assessing risks and providing technical assistance and guidance to staff throughout the agency. The person in this role will focus on agency program compliance with existing, new, and revised laws and regulations related to lead-based paint, radon, mold, asthma triggers, carbon monoxide, and other health and safety hazards. The person in this role will work closely and liaise with Offices throughout HPD, including Enforcement & Neighborhood Services (ENS), Housing Access & Stability (HAS), Asset & Property Management (APM), Development (OOD), Policy & Strategy (OPS), Finance & Administration (OFA), and Legal Affairs (OLA) for effective monitoring, tracking, and strengthening of relevant agency compliance functions.   Your Responsibilities The Compliance Specialist for Lead Hazard Control & Healthy Homes will provide agency-wide programmatic support to strengthen compliance with federal, state, and local health and safety hazard requirements. This includes, but is not limited to: •	Evaluate the implementation of lead- and healthy homes-related procedures across all areas of the agency including: o	Coordinate compliance monitoring related to requirements under federal, state, and local laws, including 24 CFR Part 35, Title X of the Residential Lead-Based Paint Hazard Reduction Act; Local Law 1 (2004), 66 (2019), Local Law 31 (2020), Local Law 111 (2023), Local Law 122 (2023), and Local Law 123 (2023), as well as Local Law 55 (2018) and other regulations related to indoor allergens such as mold and pests. o	Participate in monitoring's and/or audits Work with staff in the Offices of Enforcement & Neighborhood Services (ENS), Development, Asset & Property Management (APM), Housing Access & Stability (HAS), Neighborhood Strategies (ONS), and others to coordinate, document, and strengthen, as needed, lead and Healthy Homes hazard compliance. •	Perform assessments and evaluations to proactively identify risk areas and program noncompliance. Provide corrective action plans, recommendations, and a set of best practices, as necessary to mitigate risks. •	Participate in the development of agency-wide trainings related to lead-based paint, Healthy Homes, and other relevant healthy and safety topics. •	Support the development of internal reporting mechanisms for specialized initiatives for public reporting. •	Monitor regulatory changes and keep stakeholders abreast of operational or other implications. •	Assist with other Compliance & Strategy special projects and compliance priorities as needed. jobs.title: Data Analyst for the Division of Housing Opportunity
jobs.description: About the Agency:  The Department of Housing Preservation and Development (HPD) oversees housing standards across all 3.7 million homes in New York City.    As the nation’s largest municipal housing agency, HPD is responsible for building and preserving affordable housing, protecting tenants from harassment and displacement, and holding landlords accountable across the five boroughs. Under Commissioner Dina Levy and the Mamdani Administration, HPD is pursuing an ambitious housing agenda focused on the needs of New York’s tenants. With a broad set of tools including standards enforcement, tenant resources, and the creation of new affordable housing, HPD is committed to making New York City a more affordable place for renters and homeowners alike.   Your Team:   The Office of Housing Access and Stability (HAS) consists of the divisions of Housing Opportunities & Program Services, Tenant and Owner Resources, Housing Stability, Budget and Program Operations, and Program Policy and Innovation. Our mission of the office is to ensure fair, efficient, and transparent access to affordable housing. HAS provides subsidies, placement services, and tools that connect New Yorkers to affordable housing and ensures vulnerable households in subsidized housing have the support they need to be safely housed. Housing Access is committed to expanding housing choices, affirmatively furthering fair housing, and stabilizing the financial health of buildings.  The Division of Housing Opportunity & Program Services ensures that HPD’s affordable housing is made available through fair, transparent, and accessible programming. Developers creating affordable housing are required to offer many types of units through an open lottery process on NYC Housing Connect and fill other units through a placement process for households in the City’s shelter system. Housing Opportunity & Program Services administers the housing lottery and homeless placements programs and crafts policy and procedures to ensure that these programs offer equal opportunity to all applicants and affirmatively further fair housing.  Your Impact:  As the Data Analyst for the Homeless Placement Services (HPS) Unit within the Division of Housing Opportunity (DHO), you will support data management, reporting, performance metrics, and project intake activities for the unit, while also providing data and analytical support to the broader Division. The position will play a key role in ensuring the accuracy, timeliness, and integrity of data used to monitor HPS operations and inform program and agency decision-making. The position will also serve as a cross-functional resource for project intake and onboarding, working with managing agents and internal staff to ensure that new projects and units are properly entered, inspected, and ready for lease-up and assignment.  Your Role:  The Data Analyst will support the development, maintenance, analysis, and reporting of data related to HPS operations and DHO priorities. The position will produce and maintain reports and performance metrics used by unit and division leadership to monitor workload, production, outcomes, and operational performance. In addition, the position will support the project intake process, including entering new projects into the appropriate systems, serving as a liaison with managing agents, monitoring project readiness, and coordinating to ensure that required inspections and other prerequisites are completed before units are made available for lease-up and assignment to the HPS team. The position will also provide data and analytical support to other teams within DHO, including assisting with divisional reporting, data requests, special projects, data quality initiatives, and other analytical needs as assigned.  Your Responsibilities:  •	Maintain tracking systems and databases used to monitor HPS projects, units, assignments, referrals, placements, and other program activities. •	Generate, analyze, and distribute internal and external reports regarding unit targets, workload, production, placements, and other key performance metrics. •	Develop and maintain performance metrics and reporting tools used by HPS and DHO leadership to monitor program and operational performance. •	Analyze data to identify trends, patterns, discrepancies, and opportunities for process improvement. •	Respond to data and reporting requests from HPS and DHO leadership and staff. •	Provide data, reporting, and analytical support to other teams within DHO as needed. •	Assist with divisional data projects, reporting initiatives, special analyses, and other data-related assignments. •	Ensure data integrity and accuracy across Access, Excel, SharePoint, and other reporting and tracking systems. •	Perform routine database and reporting system maintenance to ensure alignment with changes in business processes and program requirements. •	Work with staff to identify, troubleshoot, and resolve data quality and reporting issues. •	Collaborate with staff to identify and correct data entry errors and discrepancies. •	Support the project intake process by entering new projects and related information into HPS systems and tracking platforms. •	Serve as a liaison with managing agents during the project intake and onboarding process. •	Coordinate with managing agents and internal staff to monitor project readiness and ensure required inspections and other prerequisites are completed before units are made available for lease-up and assignment to the HPS team. •	Monitor project and unit information to ensure that data is complete, accurate, and current throughout the intake and placement process. •	Coordinate and share information with the Department of Social Services (DSS) and HPD program areas to support accurate and timely referrals and placements. •	Assist with the management of a portfolio of homeless set-aside and/or 421-a homeless units, including providing referrals and tracking placements, as necessary. •	Develop and maintain documentation, procedures, and other resources supporting consistent data management, reporting, and program operations. •	Complete special projects, analyses, and reports requested by the Assistant Commissioner, Director, Deputy Director, Team Leaders, and other DHO leadership. •	Collaborate with internal and external stakeholders to resolve data, Your Team:   The Office of Development (OOD) leads the agency’s effort to create and preserve affordable housing in collaboration with other HPD offices as well as other city, state and federal agencies. The OOD is comprised of eight divisions that administer a range of programs. These divisions include New Construction Finance, Special Needs Housing, Housing Incentives, Building and Land Development Services (BLDS), Homeownership Opportunities and Preservation, Preservation Finance, Portfolio Management and Conversions, and Compliance and Enforcement.   The Division of Building and Land Development Services leads the agency’s effort in providing architectural, engineering, cost valuation, environmental planning, and construction support services to the various divisions within OOD. The Office of Development utilizes a public-private partnership model and provides loans, grants and/or incentives to assist in the finance of housing development projects that will benefit low- and moderate-income New Yorkers.   The Division of Building and Land Development Services is the largest division within the Office of Development with over 100 staff composed of seven units which include: the Bureau of New Construction Design Review Services, the Bureau of Preservation Design Review Services, the Bureau of Engineering, the Bureau of Construction Services, Environmental Planning Unit, the Policy Unit, and the Program Management Unit.     Your Impact:  As a Senior Environmental Planner, you will work with the Environmental Planning Unit and under the supervision and direction of the Director of Environmental Planning to conduct environmental assessments of new construction and rehabilitation projects in accordance with City, State and Federal environmental regulations, including reviewing site contamination assessment and investigation reports in order to build and preserve housing that is not only affordable, but also healthy and safe.  This position will contribute to the SPEED initiative (Streamlining Procedures to Expedite Equitable Development). The roles hired to advance this initiative aim to reduce timelines for the development of affordable housing through reforming four major phases of the development process: environmental review and planning, pre-development and financing, permitting and approvals, and marketing and lease-up. ABOUT KHAN ACADEMY Khan Academy is a nonprofit with the mission to deliver a free, world-class education to anyone, anywhere. Our proven learning platform offers free, high-quality supplemental learning content and practice that cover Pre-K - 12th grade and early college core academic subjects, focusing on math and science. We have over 181 million registered learners globally and are committed to improving learning outcomes for students worldwide, focusing on learners in historically under-resourced communities. ABOUT KHAN ACADEMY KIDS Khan Academy Kids is a free and fun learning program for children ages 2 to 8. Kodi Bear and a cast of animated characters lead children on a personalized education journey filled with fun, standards-aligned activities in early literacy, math, executive functioning and social emotional skills. Built by a small but mighty team, Khan Academy Kids is used by millions of children in homes and classrooms around the world. OUR COMMUNITY Our students, teachers, and parents come from all walks of life, and so do we. Our team includes people from academia, traditional/non-traditional education, big tech companies, and tiny startups. We hire great people from diverse backgrounds and experiences because it makes our company stronger. We value diversity, equity, inclusion, and belonging as necessary to achieve our mission and impact the communities we serve. We know that transforming education starts in-house with learning about ourselves and our colleagues. We strive to be world-class in investing in our people and commit to developing you as a professional. THE ROLE Khan Academy Kids is looking for a Senior Efficacy Research and Psychometrics Analyst (24 months fixed-term) to strengthen the evidence base behind our assessments and learning content for children in PreK through 2nd grade. This role spans two complementary areas. First, you will lead the technical side of our psychometrics and efficacy research: serving as the primary point of contact for our external research partners, managing recurring data extracts, analyzing and interpreting psychometric findings, and helping translate research into product improvements. Second, you will own analytics and reporting for Khan Academy Kids: building and maintaining our KPI dashboard and preparing the recurring reporting that our leadership, philanthropy, and school partnerships teams rely on to make decisions and tell our impact story. You will work on a small, interdisciplinary team alongside product managers, engineers, designers, and academic experts and collaborate closely with leading external research organizations. We are looking for someone with strong quantitative training — ideally in psychometrics, educational measurement, or a related field — who is energized by using rigorous evidence to improve learning experiences for young children. Responsibilities: (1) Psychometrics & Efficacy Research Lead our psychometric research partnership : Serve as the primary technical point of contact for our external psychometric research partnership, supporting study design, data sharing, psychometric analyses, and interpretation of findings Extract, clean, and securely share assessment data with research partners on a recurring schedule Analyze and interpret psychometric findings, including item difficulty, score distributions, growth analyses, concurrent validity, and IRT-based scoring Partner with our product and engineering teams to translate findings into product improvements, such as updates to scoring models and assessment discontinuation rules Collaborate with research partners to develop and publish technical documentation, beginning with the technical manual for our PreK assessment Recruit and manage research partner sites: Recruit and onboard school and district sites for psychometric and efficacy studies; execute MOUs; align on consent procedures and participant incentives; and coordinate site visits for direct child assessment data collection Partner with our legal team to draft and negotiate data-sharing agreements with districts and research organizations, including requirements for pseudonymized and identified data Support efficacy research. Coordinate Khan Academy Kids' participation in ongoing efficacy studies and contribute to the design of future studies, aligning internal and external stakeholders on the research approach (2) Analytics Reporting and Data Infrastructure Own Khan Kids’s KPI dashboard: Partner with our engineering team to build and maintain the Khan Academy Kids analytics dashboard, including integrations with App Store Connect and Google Play Console. Maintain the dashboard so it can be used by other teams including marketing, school partnerships, and philanthropy. Lead recurring reporting: Prepare recurring app performance reporting, including monthly and quarterly business reviews and periodic target setting. Field ad hoc data requests across teams — for example, writing new SQL queries to support targeted district outreach or grant reporting. jobs.title: Senior Data Engineer
jobs.description:
About Kiddom

Kiddom is transforming K–12 education by bringing high-quality curriculum, instructional tools, and student analytics together in one coherent system. We are building Learning Intelligence Technology (LIT), a new category that gives educators the infrastructure to plan, teach, assess, and respond to student needs. With Kiddom, educators spend less time managing administrative burden and more time delivering meaningful student instruction. Kiddom helps schools and districts deliver more equitable, effective, and adaptive learning experiences.

We're looking for a Senior Data Engineer to join Kiddom's Content & AI Systems team, building the data layer that powers next-generation AI-assisted curriculum authoring and content delivery. You'll own the pipelines, schemas, and validation frameworks that turn messy, domain-specific curriculum content into structured, AI-ready data products, working closely with Instructional Designers, AI engineers, and the Content Agents team. This role suits an engineer who's comfortable in a non-traditional data engineering space and energized by defining data requirements and infrastructure from the ground up.


You will:

 - Design and own the schema and data models representing Kiddom’s curriculum content (lessons, activities, standards alignments) for downstream use 

 - Build ingestion pipelines that process content from varied, inconsistent source formats — XML, JSON, PDF-derived, and API-delivered

 - Develop Python-based parsers, transformers, and validation scripts that enforce schema conformance and content quality at scale 

 - Collaborate directly with Instructional Designers and product teams to translate content authoring workflows into data engineering requirements

 - Build and maintain embedding and vector database pipelines that feed Kiddom’s AI-powered content features as they scale

 - Work in Git-based workflows — treating data artifacts with the same rigor as software: versioned, reviewed, and documented

What we're looking for:

 - 4+ years of data engineering experience with strong Python skills — you’ve written parsers, validators, and transformation scripts for real-world messy data

 - Schema design instincts — you think carefully about how data should be structured for downstream use, not just how to move it 

 - Data quality mindset — you build validation and completeness checks in from the start, not as an afterthought 

 - Cross-functional collaborator — comfortable working with non-engineers to define requirements and translate domain knowledge into data structures

 - Provisioning and monitoring of infrastructure for data systems, familiarity with IaC tools such as Terraform and Terragrunt

 - The data system operates, ECS, EKS clusters, provision lambdas and S3 buckets

 - Bachelor’s or Master’s degree in CS or equivalent work experience

Nice to Have: 

 - Background in education, curriculum design, or ed-tech — understanding how instructional content is authored and structured is a genuine differentiator

 - Experience with vector databases (Pinecone, Weaviate, pgvector) or embedding pipeline tooling 

 - Familiarity with agentic AI patterns or Model Context Protocol (MCP)

 

What we offer

 - Full time permanent employees are eligible for the following benefits from their first day of employment:

 - Competitive salary

 - Meaningful equity

 - Health insurance benefits: medical (various PPO/HMO/HSA plans), dental, vision, disability and life insurance

 - 401k plan

 - One Medical membership (in participating locations)

 - Flexible vacation time policy (subject to internal approval). Average use 4 weeks off per year.

 - 10 paid sick days per year (pro rated depending on start date)

 - Paid holidays

 - Paid bereavement leave

 - Paid family leave after birth/adoption. Minimum of 16 paid weeks for birthing parents, 10 weeks for caretaker parents. Meant to supplement benefits offered by State.

 - Commuter and FSA plans


Equal Employment Opportunity Policy

Kiddom is committed to providing equal employment opportunities to all employees and applicants without regard to race, religion, color, gender, sexual orientation, transgender status, national origin, citizenship status, uniform service member status, pregnancy, age, genetic information, disability, or any other protected status in accordance with all applicable federal, state, and local laws.

Mathematica offers our employees competitive salaries, and a comprehensive benefits package, as well as the advantages of being 100 percent employee owned. Learn more about our benefits here. At Mathematica, we take pride in our commitment to diversity. We are looking for a Data Scientist who will derive meaning from data through the creation and deployment of data-driven approaches to solve problems and answer important policy questions for clients. A Data Scientist owns data processing and analysis tasks and supports more senior level data science staff in implementing statistical, machine learning, generative AI, and other data science methods for use in research reports, internal systems, or client systems. Data Scientists will work on all aspects of the data science project life cycle, including understanding client needs, building data pipelines, monitoring data quality, developing documentation, creating visualizations, brainstorming modeling approaches, and implementing those models. Our data scientists underpin our company's core offerings in program improvement, policy assessment, and data science, which yield crucial evidence and information for policy and decision makers. This position will work remotely or flexibly in one of our office locations. The ideal candidate for this open Data Science position has a strong interest in applying their skills to healthcare and a strong statistical background in causal inference and supporting methodologies such as imputation, matching, weighting, regression, quasi-experimental methods, and synthetic-comparison methods, among others. In addition to the required technical skills below, our healthcare-focused data scientists strongly benefit from additional knowledge of SQL or Scala, experience with big data analysis platforms such as Databricks or Snowflake, and familiarity with healthcare datasets such as Medicare or Medicaid claims and enrollment data and electronic medical records. Example projects include: Evaluate and monitor the impacts of an alternative payment model for primary care in terms of care quality, cost, and health outcomes for diverse beneficiaries, using claims from thousands of primary care practices across the country. Use the same data to predict future hospital costs and behavior. Develop and evaluate a reproducible benchmarking pipeline to compare state healthcare spending against peer markets nationwide, harmonizing multi-source claims and Census data, applying statistical matching to select comparable regions, and normalizing spending through risk-adjusted regression models to support state rate-setting decisions. Build and evaluate interpretable machine learning models to predict clinical care tiers from health assessment data, supporting state healthcare program's transition to a new assessment tool. Partner with subject-matter experts to engineer clinically meaningful features from raw assessment items and apply stratified sampling and diagnostics to deliver transparent models suited to high-stakes eligibility and reimbursement decisions Specifically, this Data Scientist contributes to team-based projects by: Conducting causal, predictive, and descriptive analyses Writing and maintaining programming systems in languages such as Python and R to build and evaluate models Developing reliable data pipelines to obtain, combine, and transform datasets on cloud, internal, and client servers Communicating technical results to diverse stakeholders including clients and cross-functional teams Developing and maintaining technical and methodological documentation Co-developing analysis plans with a senior data scientist or researcher Leading and managing small teams and tasks with oversight from a more senior staff member
